chesterton_fence_comment_edited.name: 'Do not remove / order matters' fence later changed or broken
chesterton_fence_comment_edited.label: Pattern
chesterton_fence_comment_edited.pitfall: Invariant comments are deleted in refactors.
chesterton_fence_comment_edited.signal: Added lines matching do not (remove|change|reorder)|order matters|must be called before|workaround for|load-bearing; guarded lines (next 5 or symbol) later changed; rank fix/revert within 90 days; lower tier plain modification; also surface unviolated fences.
chesterton_fence_comment_edited.packet: Fence, intro commit, guarded lines before/after, follow-up, tests.
chesterton_fence_comment_edited.question: What invariant and was it violated?
chesterton_fence_comment_edited.noise: Vendored/generated, sort-order prose, documented removals, TODO-only.
chesterton_fence_comment_edited.example: 'DO NOT sort' replaced by sorted(); hotfix follows.

locking_ddl_on_hot_table.name: Blocking DDL on a high-churn table
locking_ddl_on_hot_table.label: AntiPattern
locking_ddl_on_hot_table.pitfall: Non-concurrent index, NOT NULL, type change take strong locks.
locking_ddl_on_hot_table.why: Fine in dev, outage at production size.
locking_ddl_on_hot_table.signal: Migration diffs with blocking DDL forms (negatives: CONCURRENTLY, NOT VALID, lock_timeout); table exists in earlier migration; weight by table heat; require later rewrite/revert/lock_timeout/lock fix or high heat; rank by those.
locking_ddl_on_hot_table.packet: Migration diff, engine, other migrations on table, later fixes.
locking_ddl_on_hot_table.question: Safe at production size; what multi-step rule emerged?
locking_ddl_on_hot_table.example: CREATE INDEX on 200M rows without CONCURRENTLY.

fix_without_regression_test.name: Bug fix shipped without a regression test
fix_without_regression_test.label: AntiPattern
fix_without_regression_test.pitfall: A fix lands with no test that fails on the old code, so the bug can return silently and often does.
fix_without_regression_test.why: Fix commits are ground-truth defect locations (SZZ). Past fixes predict future ones (Kim et al.). Covrig found a minority of corrective commits touch tests. The fix diff states exactly what the missing test should assert. Oracle's fix lineage has regression_tests data but nothing ranks the absence.
fix_without_regression_test.signal: Per fix F in the fix lineage: production hunk in a function body, no test file touched and no test function added in F or within +-7 days on the same branch or author, and at HEAD the symbol has no static-call test link (weight>=0.6) that changed after F. Add a sibling trigger: a commit that deletes or empties a test function while its target symbol survives at HEAD (test erosion). Skip fixes where commit message matches typo/docs/lint/format/deps, hunks under 2 changed lines without a branch or guard, and fixes whose symbol was deleted. Rank by zone weight x repeat count x fan_in percentile.
fix_without_regression_test.packet: Fix message and function-scoped diff; zone; presence/absence of test files in window; test-map links at HEAD (source, weight); later commits on the symbol; linked issue/PR text; coverage flags for fix lines if imported.
fix_without_regression_test.question: What input and expected-vs-actual would have failed before the fix? Is it unit-testable cheaply or needs an integration seam? Name file, function, arrange/act/assert. Say if it was a one-off typo that cannot recur.
fix_without_regression_test.noise: Docs, typo, comment, formatting, lint, dependency, config-only and lockfile fixes; bulk commits; code deleted at HEAD; fixes only to tests; one-line import fixes without guards; fixes whose lines are fully covered at HEAD.
fix_without_regression_test.example: e220ae2 'Fix MCP hang on Windows: empty stdin' added stdin=DEVNULL; no test asserts the stdin argument. A test patching subprocess.run and asserting stdin is DEVNULL at every call site is the guard.
sources: Sliwerski, Zimmermann, Zeller, When Do Changes Induce Fixes?, MSR 2005
Kochhar et al., Code coverage and postrelease defects, IEEE Trans. Reliability 2017
Winters et al., Software Engineering at Google ch.11 (Beyonce Rule)
Feathers, Working Effectively with Legacy Code, 2004

fix_on_fix_chain.name: Chain of fixes to the same lines
fix_on_fix_chain.label: Pattern
fix_on_fix_chain.pitfall: Repeated fixes of one region show a misunderstood invariant.
fix_on_fix_chain.why: Turns a chain into 'the real requirement is X'.
fix_on_fix_chain.signal: >=3 fix-class commits (each >=3 code lines) on the same symbol or blame-overlapping lines within 60 days, or later fix removes lines added by earlier fix. Rank 'again/still/properly' messages; boost race/security zones.
fix_on_fix_chain.packet: Ordered chain diffs, messages, gaps, tests.
fix_on_fix_chain.question: What did each fix miss; what is the final invariant?
fix_on_fix_chain.noise: Skip same-PR series (<1h), format/typo, lockfiles, generated.
fix_on_fix_chain.example: Three fixes in 10 days to one pagination off-by-one.

commit_message_signal_hack_workaround.name: Commit message states a constraint or incident whose code survives
commit_message_signal_hack_workaround.label: Pattern
commit_message_signal_hack_workaround.pitfall: Messages carry reasons absent from code and later cleanup reintroduces the issue.
commit_message_signal_hack_workaround.why: Turns commit graph into an incident-scar registry.
commit_message_signal_hack_workaround.signal: Message regex (workaround|hack|do not (remove|change)|must come first|otherwise it breaks|upstream bug|SEV|outage); >=3 added lines survive (hunk lineage) without >=5-word comment; require explicit-constraint phrase or incident token; boost config/infra and later edits not citing the reason.
commit_message_signal_hack_workaround.packet: Full message, hunk, current code, issue, later commits.
commit_message_signal_hack_workaround.question: What unstated constraint does this satisfy; still needed?
commit_message_signal_hack_workaround.noise: Skip removed lines, tests/docs, bot bumps, bare #123 refs.
commit_message_signal_hack_workaround.example: 'work around pip resolver bug; do not reorder' then cleanup reorders and build fails.

pinned_dependency_with_reason.name: Dependency pin, cap or override with a recorded reason
pinned_dependency_with_reason.label: Pattern
pinned_dependency_with_reason.pitfall: Pins and overrides dodge an upstream break and are never revisited.
pinned_dependency_with_reason.why: Upgrades hit the same break; obsolete pins block security fixes.
pinned_dependency_with_reason.signal: Manifest diffs adding <,<=,~=,==,!= or override/resolutions/replace/[patch] where message or adjacent comment matches pin|cap|lock|downgrade|break|incompatible|workaround|CVE, or range becomes pin after build fix. Rank pins >12 months with callers.
pinned_dependency_with_reason.packet: Pin diff, message, usage sites, pin history.
pinned_dependency_with_reason.question: What failed and what must be true to lift the pin?
pinned_dependency_with_reason.noise: Skip bot bumps, lockfile regen, local replace paths.
pinned_dependency_with_reason.example: pydantic<2 added with 'v2 breaks validators', still there 18 months later.

tunable_knob_churn.name: Operational tunable repeatedly re-tuned
tunable_knob_churn.label: Pattern
tunable_knob_churn.pitfall: Timeouts, retries, pools, TTLs are edited repeatedly after incidents.
tunable_knob_churn.why: Value history records cliff edges (metastable failures).
tunable_knob_churn.signal: Track numeric (file,key) values for timeout|retries|backoff|pool|batch_size|ttl|rate_limit|concurrency|replicas|memory in code and config; >=3 distinct values, A->B->A, or >=2x change; require a message/fix-lineage reason; boost outage words.
tunable_knob_churn.packet: Value series with SHA/date/author/message, neighbours, call sites.
tunable_knob_churn.question: What justified each value and what is the safe range?
tunable_knob_churn.noise: Exclude version/port/ID keys, bot bumps, tests, single introductions.

false_test_gap.name: 'No test' verdict contradicted by history (test_gap audit)
false_test_gap.label: AntiPattern
false_test_gap.pitfall: Believing the binary test_gap risk factor. Gaps drive assess_change output, so false gaps waste effort and teach users to ignore the tool; conversely a test repeatedly co-edited in fixes of unlinked code reveals hidden coupling.
false_test_gap.why: The map has only approximate links without coverage data; cross-checking each gap against the repo's own behaviour history is a cheap sanity check before recommending tests. Coverage quantity is a weak proxy for effectiveness (Inozemtseva and Holmes), and pair-level fix co-edit evidence mirrors learned test-to-change edges (Facebook predictive test selection).
false_test_gap.signal: Symbols with test_gap=true and risk >= 80th percentile, plus >=2 distinct non-bulk fix commits. Evidence level 0 = no test co-edit in any fix (genuinely untested, recommend a test, cite the fixed behaviours as the cases); 1 = a test edited in >=1 fix of the symbol; 2 = the same test edited in >=2 fixes; 3 = a test importing a caller within 2 hops edited in >=30% of the symbol's commits. Require the T hunk to touch an assert, expected literal or setup line. Exclude symbols <5 lines, dunders, property getters, generated or vendored code. Output both directions: truly-untested-and-risky (priority) and falsely-gapped (map correction).
false_test_gap.packet: Symbol body and risk breakdown; fix/co-edit commit list with test files and zones; test hunks; 2-hop call path from candidate tests; current map links (null result) for both sides; T's imports and calls.
false_test_gap.question: Is it really untested or covered indirectly? If indirect, which test and does it assert the behaviours the fixes changed; is T a real guard of S or a coincidence via a shared fixture? If truly untested, what exact test (inputs, expected output) to add, or which history_fix link should be recorded?
false_test_gap.noise: Symbols <5 lines, dunders, property getters, generated/vendored; only-bulk-commit co-edits; pairs sharing only helpers, conftest, snapshot or lockfile edits; require the T hunk to touch an assert, expected literal or setup line.
false_test_gap.example: parse_retry_after has test_gap = true and 3 fixes; all 3 also edited tests/test_http_client.py via fetch(). Indirectly covered but only 200 and 429 paths asserted; add a direct test with header absent. tests/test_cli.py edited in 4 fixes of core/scheduler.py is its only guard.
sources: Inozemtseva and Holmes, Coverage is not strongly correlated with test suite effectiveness, ICSE 2014
Ivankovic et al., Code coverage at Google, FSE 2019
Machalica et al., Predictive Test Selection, ICSE-SEIP 2019
Zaidman et al., Mining software repositories to study co-evolution of production and test code, STVR 2011

clone_sibling_fix_divergence.name: Bug fixed in one clone but not its near-duplicate siblings
clone_sibling_fix_divergence.label: AntiPattern
clone_sibling_fix_divergence.pitfall: Fixes applied to one copy-paste clone leave siblings defective.
clone_sibling_fix_divergence.why: Points to a likely live bug with an immediate action.
clone_sibling_fix_divergence.signal: Fix commit hunk (>=2 nontrivial removed lines) in a symbol in an idiom_cluster (sim>=0.8); sibling not changed within 60 days still literally contains the pre-fix lines (whitespace-normalised). One packet per fix, rank by sibling fan-in.
clone_sibling_fix_divergence.packet: Fix diff, sibling bodies with matches marked, sibling diary, callers.
clone_sibling_fix_divergence.question: Does the sibling share the defect or is divergence deliberate?
clone_sibling_fix_divergence.noise: Drop tests, generated, dead siblings, comment/format fixes, <6-line snippets.
clone_sibling_fix_divergence.example: Null-check fix in parse_user_v1 while copy parse_account stays unchecked.

ci_gate_weakening.name: CI/CD gate disabled, loosened or made non-blocking
ci_gate_weakening.label: AntiPattern
ci_gate_weakening.pitfall: Tests, scans, coverage gates are skipped or lowered and never restored.
ci_gate_weakening.signal: Added continue-on-error/allow_failure/if:false/fail_under decrease in a step matching test|lint|type|scan|coverage; score message skip|unblock|temporarily|flaky; rank never restored and repeated lowering.
ci_gate_weakening.question: What was failing and is it still disabled?
ci_gate_weakening.noise: Nightly/experimental, fork-only, bulk refactors, initial scaffolding.

pseudo_tested_function.name: Executed but unasserted (pseudo-tested) function
pseudo_tested_function.label: AntiPattern
pseudo_tested_function.pitfall: Tests reach a function (links, coverage) but assert nothing meaningful on its result, so any gutted body still passes.
pseudo_tested_function.why: Pseudo-tested methods exist in every studied project; checked coverage beats statement coverage (Schuler & Zeller); Oracle's binary test_gap reads these as safe.
pseudo_tested_function.signal: Phase 1: a test function with zero assertion constructs (assert, self.assert*, expect(, pytest.raises, mock.assert_*, and calls to local helpers whose names start with assert/check/verify/expect) after one-hop helper expansion. Target symbol: every linked test is such a test, and the symbol has >=1 fix commit or fan_in>=5 or risk>=60. Exclude smoke/import/does_not_raise/main tests, doctests, snapshots, and property-based tests. Phase 2, only after review of results: add weak-only assertions (assert True, is not None, toBeDefined).
pseudo_tested_function.packet: Target body and return paths; each test body with assertion inventory and link weight; fix commits and guards; coverage; mutation survivors; sibling strong tests.
pseudo_tested_function.question: Would any plausible regression (wrong return, dropped side effect, swallowed error) fail these tests? Name the assertion that would have failed under past fixes. Or is it an acceptable smoke test?
pseudo_tested_function.noise: Tests named smoke/import/starts/does_not_raise, CLI main smoke tests; tests asserting via helpers/fixtures or pytest.raises/mock.assert_called; void side-effect-free wrappers; snapshot and doctest tests; property-based tests; trivial getters.
pseudo_tested_function.example: test_export calls export_report() and asserts nothing; export_report has 3 fixes adding None-guards. Assert row count and header.
sources: Vera-Perez et al., Pseudo-tested methods, EMSE 2019

public_api_breaking_change.name: Public API break and version-bump mismatch
public_api_breaking_change.label: Pattern
public_api_breaking_change.why: Downstream runtime failures and lost migration path.
public_api_breaking_change.signal: Diff public API surface (exported via __all__/package root) between tags or version-bump commits; removed symbols/params; break with patch/minor bump or reverted/fixed within 14 days; rank by caller counts.
public_api_breaking_change.packet: Surface diff, callers, CHANGELOG, bump type.
public_api_breaking_change.question: Intentional and documented?
public_api_breaking_change.example: Patch release removes public function; yanked next day.

renamed_path_still_referenced_in_tooling.name: Renamed path still referenced by tooling configs
renamed_path_still_referenced_in_tooling.label: AntiPattern
renamed_path_still_referenced_in_tooling.pitfall: CODEOWNERS, CI filters, COPY, coverage config keep old paths.
renamed_path_still_referenced_in_tooling.signal: Rename lineage with old path absent at HEAD; path-boundary token match in CODEOWNERS/.github/Dockerfile/Makefile/yaml/toml/scripts not touched by rename commit; skip if old path prefixes existing path; rank CODEOWNERS/CI/COPY first.
renamed_path_still_referenced_in_tooling.packet: Rename commit, reference lines, later fixes.
renamed_path_still_referenced_in_tooling.question: Which references are stale?

reopened_same_symbol_fix_cadence.name: Symbol fixed repeatedly (chronic bug site)
reopened_same_symbol_fix_cadence.label: AntiPattern
reopened_same_symbol_fix_cadence.pitfall: Same function accumulates fixes, indicating a design flaw.
reopened_same_symbol_fix_cadence.why: Past fixes predict future defects; extracts the recurring theme.
reopened_same_symbol_fix_cadence.signal: Symbols alive at HEAD with >=4 fix commits modifying the body (>=40% with >2 changed lines) over >=3 months or >=3 authors; fix share >=0.4. Cap packet to 5 recent and 2 largest diffs.
reopened_same_symbol_fix_cadence.question: What missing invariant explains repeated fixes?
reopened_same_symbol_fix_cadence.noise: Exclude generated, tests, tables, typo fixes, dispatchers.
reopened_same_symbol_fix_cadence.example: BugCache found 73-95% of faults in 10% of files.

test_deleted_behavior_kept.name: Test deleted while the behaviour it guarded stayed
test_deleted_behavior_kept.label: AntiPattern
test_deleted_behavior_kept.pitfall: A test (or assertions) removed alone while the production function it exercised is alive and changing; the safety net vanishes.
test_deleted_behavior_kept.why: Many deletions are not obsolescence (Pinto 2012); 83% of deleted tests go with their whole class so a lone deletion is informative (MSR 2025); deleted-to-pass-CI.
test_deleted_behavior_kept.signal: Test symbol deleted or assertion count down >=50% in non-bulk commit C. Name-match target (test_foo -> foo) exists at C^ and at HEAD, not renamed in C. No same-name or >=0.8-similar test at HEAD. Rank by later fixes on target after C and by age. Use a cheap regex assertion count on the diary body.
test_deleted_behavior_kept.packet: Deleted test body and assertions; commit C message/diff and target changes; target diary; links before/after; later fixes; same-name or similar-body test elsewhere.
test_deleted_behavior_kept.question: Behaviour dropped, test redundant/flaky, or merely inconvenient? Which assertions should be restored and would a later fix have been caught?
test_deleted_behavior_kept.noise: Target deleted/renamed in same commit; replacement with >=0.8 body similarity or equal static link; parametrize rewrites preserving assertion count; targets deleted within 30 days; bulk commits; tests moved between files.
test_deleted_behavior_kept.example: test_fetch_none (asserting ValueError) deleted in 'speed up CI'; fetch() keeps the guard and got two later fixes.
sources: Understanding Test Deletion in Java Applications, MSR 2025

proven_guard_test.name: Test edited in many fixes (proven regression catcher) and its under-tested siblings
proven_guard_test.label: AntiPattern
proven_guard_test.pitfall: Deleting, rewriting, mocking or rubber-stamping a test with a history of encoding fixed bugs, and not noticing its structurally similar siblings lack the same rigor.
proven_guard_test.why: Per-test fault history is what Google TAP and Elbaum et al. use to prioritise and protect tests; this tells the user what not to touch and which test is the template for the next one.
proven_guard_test.signal: Test functions edited in at least 3 distinct fix commits, each with a production-code change in the same commit (not bulk, not rename-only), where at least one hunk adds or changes an assert, expect or parametrize line. Siblings are symbols in the same module with at least 2 fix commits where no linked test was edited in those fixes, or whose linked tests have assert count 0 or 1. Rank by distinct fixes, then by the sibling's fix count. Packet: the test body, per-fix subject and zone, and the top 3 siblings with their fix lists.
proven_guard_test.packet: Test body; per-fix classified diffs with subjects and zones; target symbols and assertion depth; zero-edit neighbours of similar risk.
proven_guard_test.question: What behaviours does this test pin per its fixes? Which siblings share the bug shape without a similar test, and what is the one test to write next and what does it assert?
proven_guard_test.noise: Test edits in test-only commits, bulk/merge commits, rename/format edits; require production change in same commit.
proven_guard_test.example: test_parse_duration gained a case in 4 fixes (negative, overflow, locale comma, empty); sibling parse_size has 2 fixes and one happy-path test. Add a parametrized test with the same four classes.
sources: Elbaum, Rothermel and Penix, Techniques for improving regression testing in continuous integration development environments, FSE 2014
Vahabzadeh, Stocco and Mesbah, An empirical study of bugs in test code, ICSME 2015

trusted_proxy_trust_setting_change.name: Trusted-proxy / forwarded-header trust changed
trusted_proxy_trust_setting_change.label: Pattern
trusted_proxy_trust_setting_change.pitfall: Wrong trust values spoof IPs or break scheme detection.
trusted_proxy_trust_setting_change.why: Value depends on hop count invisible in code.
trusted_proxy_trust_setting_change.signal: Changed lines with trust proxy|FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS|ProxyFix|SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER|set_real_ip_from|KnownProxies etc. where value token (true,'*',int,CIDR) differs between -/+; rank later fixes on same key and proxy/loop/ip/https messages.
trusted_proxy_trust_setting_change.question: What topology does this assume?
trusted_proxy_trust_setting_change.example: trust proxy true lets clients spoof X-Forwarded-For.

keep_in_sync_partner_unchanged.name: 'Keep in sync with X' where X drifted
keep_in_sync_partner_unchanged.label: Pattern
keep_in_sync_partner_unchanged.signal: Annotation regex resolved exactly to partner path/identifier; host changed >=3 commits since with partner moved in fewer than half within 7 days, or partner dangling; divergence visible in content (enum members); suppress high-Jaccard pairs.
keep_in_sync_partner_unchanged.question: What must stay equal?
keep_in_sync_partner_unchanged.noise: External URLs, deleted files, already-reported pairs.
keep_in_sync_partner_unchanged.example: Python enum gains members; TS types.ts not.

app_keepalive_502_fix_lineage.name: App keep-alive/idle-timeout changed for 502/ECONNRESET
app_keepalive_502_fix_lineage.label: Pattern
app_keepalive_502_fix_lineage.pitfall: App keep-alive must outlast LB idle timeout.
app_keepalive_502_fix_lineage.signal: Keep-alive-family key change (keepAliveTimeout, headersTimeout, --keep-alive, idle_timeout) with symptom words (502|504|ECONNRESET|bad gateway) in message, +/-5 commits or linked PR title; also settings dropped by framework migration.
app_keepalive_502_fix_lineage.packet: Diff, message, proxy config, later edits.
app_keepalive_502_fix_lineage.question: Which two timeouts must keep ordering?
app_keepalive_502_fix_lineage.example: keepAliveTimeout=65000 fixes ALB 502s; migration drops it.

migration_edited_after_commit.name: Applied migration file edited after creation
migration_edited_after_commit.label: AntiPattern
migration_edited_after_commit.pitfall: Editing merged migrations diverges environments and breaks checksums.
migration_edited_after_commit.signal: Migration path with non-whitespace, non-comment modify >24h after creation or tag, creator on mainline; boost checksum/drift messages or follow-up migration on same table.
migration_edited_after_commit.question: Was an applied migration rewritten?

backfill_job_rerun_scars.name: Backfill/data-fix job edited repeatedly after run
backfill_job_rerun_scars.label: Pattern
backfill_job_rerun_scars.pitfall: Backfills gain batching and idempotency guards after failed runs.
backfill_job_rerun_scars.why: Scars form a checklist for next data job.
backfill_job_rerun_scars.signal: Path/name-matched data jobs with >=3 commits where >=2 distinct guard categories (batch, cursor, idempotent, throttle, dry_run, timeouts) added across separate commits; sub-signal: data statement lacking guard later added.
backfill_job_rerun_scars.packet: Chronological diffs, tables touched, sibling backfills.
backfill_job_rerun_scars.question: What guard set must new backfills include?
backfill_job_rerun_scars.example: backfill_user_slugs gains batching, cursor, conflict skip.

fragile_base_class_override_drift.name: Base method contract changed while overrides keep old form
fragile_base_class_override_drift.label: AntiPattern
fragile_base_class_override_drift.pitfall: Fragile base class: overrides go stale in dynamic languages.
fragile_base_class_override_drift.signal: INHERITS + diary: base method param add/remove/reorder/rename or hook call added/removed; HEAD overrides whose params equal old base signature, not touched since the change; rank by override count and base-typed call sites.
fragile_base_class_override_drift.question: Are overrides invoked incorrectly or dead?
fragile_base_class_override_drift.noise: Single implementer changed in commit, test doubles.

dockerfile_base_image_aftermath.name: Base-image change aftermath
dockerfile_base_image_aftermath.label: RejectedAttempt
dockerfile_base_image_aftermath.pitfall: FROM changes (alpine/debian, majors) cause libc/cert/wheel fallout and reverts.
dockerfile_base_image_aftermath.signal: FROM re-switch/revert within 180 days, or distro-family/major change followed by >=2 build/runtime/package fixes within 30 days; COPY-before-install etc. secondary.
dockerfile_base_image_aftermath.question: Why this base and what failed before?
dockerfile_base_image_aftermath.noise: Skip test Dockerfiles, bot bumps in family.
dockerfile_base_image_aftermath.example: slim to alpine reverted: wheels compile from source.

ci_path_filter_new_dir_gap.name: CI path filter does not cover changed code
ci_path_filter_new_dir_gap.label: AntiPattern
ci_path_filter_new_dir_gap.pitfall: Path filters are not updated when new source dirs appear.
ci_path_filter_new_dir_gap.why: Code ships with zero CI signal.
ci_path_filter_new_dir_gap.signal: Parse workflow paths/paths-ignore/rules:changes; commit uncovered only if no push/PR workflow on default branch matches (require a test-like workflow); >=3 commits or one adding >=3 files; boost later filter edit.
ci_path_filter_new_dir_gap.packet: Filter block, uncovered commits, first-commit date of dir.
ci_path_filter_new_dir_gap.question: Does uncovered code have CI elsewhere?
ci_path_filter_new_dir_gap.noise: Docs, assets, generated, other unfiltered workflow.

ci_privilege_and_trigger_widening.name: CI permissions, triggers or action pinning widened
ci_privilege_and_trigger_widening.label: AntiPattern
ci_privilege_and_trigger_widening.pitfall: pull_request_target, write-all, unpinned actions expose secrets.
ci_privilege_and_trigger_widening.why: CI is a supply-chain surface (tj-actions CVE-2025-30066).
ci_privilege_and_trigger_widening.signal: Added risky trigger/permission (pull_request_target, write-all, secrets: inherit, self-hosted, @main replacing SHA, github.event in run:); boost pull_request_target with PR-head checkout; SHA pin reverted to tag.
ci_privilege_and_trigger_widening.question: Does it expose secrets to untrusted code?
ci_privilege_and_trigger_widening.noise: Drop actions/*, read-only, private repos without forks.

cors_policy_change_history.name: CORS policy widened, narrowed or oscillating
cors_policy_change_history.label: AntiPattern
cors_policy_change_history.pitfall: Wildcard/reflected origins and unanchored regexes with credentials.
cors_policy_change_history.why: Cross-site authenticated reads; narrowing breaks partners.
cors_policy_change_history.signal: Added wildcard/true, allow_credentials with non-literal origin, regex/endswith/includes origin match, or origin key changed >=3 commits; suppress localhost-only.
cors_policy_change_history.packet: CORS timeline, app and proxy layers, auth mechanism.
cors_policy_change_history.question: Is policy safe for credentialed requests?
cors_policy_change_history.noise: Public unauthenticated APIs, repeated single-domain additions.

legacy_persisted_name_pinned.name: Code renamed but persisted name pinned to legacy
legacy_persisted_name_pinned.label: Pattern
legacy_persisted_name_pinned.pitfall: Mapping literals keep old names after renames.
legacy_persisted_name_pinned.why: Renaming the literal breaks rows or consumers.
legacy_persisted_name_pinned.signal: Diary shows symbol rename with persistence literal (db_column, @Column(name), serialized_name, alias, __tablename__) unchanged or newly added in that commit; skip mere case/underscore differences without rename.
legacy_persisted_name_pinned.packet: Field, rename diff, other usages of literal.
legacy_persisted_name_pinned.question: Is the legacy name a frozen contract?
legacy_persisted_name_pinned.example: owner_id keeps db_column='usr_id'; warehouse reads it.

confessed_ignorance_comment_live_code.name: Comments admitting nobody knows why code exists
confessed_ignorance_comment_live_code.label: AntiPattern
confessed_ignorance_comment_live_code.pitfall: 'not sure why' marks lost knowledge in live code.
confessed_ignorance_comment_live_code.signal: Comments: not sure why|no idea why|for historical reasons|don't touch|nobody knows|why does this work; fan-in >=3 or >=2 later fixes; introducing author inactive >12 months; skip TODO/FIXME.
confessed_ignorance_comment_live_code.question: Can the reason be reconstructed?
confessed_ignorance_comment_live_code.example: 'not sure why this sleep is needed' called from 14 sites.

magic_constant_comment_divergence.name: Constant whose comment or cited spec no longer matches
magic_constant_comment_divergence.label: Pattern
magic_constant_comment_divergence.pitfall: Constants change without their rationale comment.
magic_constant_comment_divergence.signal: Changed numeric literal adjacent to untouched comment containing old value (incl. 30s/24h forms) or authority citation (RFC|SLA|policy|GDPR|PCI); edit-count variant only with authority regex.
magic_constant_comment_divergence.question: Which is authoritative?
magic_constant_comment_divergence.noise: Tables, fixtures, versions, ports, same-commit comment edits.
magic_constant_comment_divergence.example: SESSION_TTL 1800 '30 min per policy 4.2' changed to 3600.

resurrected_deleted_code.name: Deleted file or symbol later restored
resurrected_deleted_code.label: RejectedAttempt
resurrected_deleted_code.pitfall: Code removed as obsolete is later reintroduced; a hidden consumer was missed.
resurrected_deleted_code.why: Records what depended on it (Chesterton's fence).
resurrected_deleted_code.signal: Diary: symbol deleted then recreated >=3 days later with body similarity >=0.85, >=10 lines, same name or blob; >=1 intervening commit; exclude reverts, merges, cherry-picks. Rank by intervening fixes.
resurrected_deleted_code.packet: Deleting and restoring commits, diff, interval, fixes.
resurrected_deleted_code.question: What consumer was missed?
resurrected_deleted_code.example: legacy_export() removed; restored two weeks later when a monthly job fails.

dependency_downgrade_or_revert.name: Dependency upgrade reverted or downgraded
dependency_downgrade_or_revert.label: RejectedAttempt
dependency_downgrade_or_revert.pitfall: Upgrades are reverted for breakage and later repeated.
dependency_downgrade_or_revert.why: Revert reason is a rejected-attempt record.
dependency_downgrade_or_revert.signal: Direct manifest deps (not lockfile transitives): A->B->A or lower within 120 days via per-ecosystem version parser, or commit reverting the bump; weight majors; drop prerelease and range-widening.
dependency_downgrade_or_revert.question: Why did upgrade fail?
dependency_downgrade_or_revert.example: webpack 4 to 5 then revert: breaks CSS loader.

deprecated_never_removed.name: Deprecated API still gaining callers
deprecated_never_removed.label: Pattern
deprecated_never_removed.pitfall: Deprecated symbols persist and new callers copy the deprecated form.
deprecated_never_removed.why: Assistants copy the trap; replacement is lost.
deprecated_never_removed.signal: @deprecated/warnings.warn(Deprecat)/OpenAPI deprecated; primary tier: >=2 call sites created after deprecation commit and replacement named; low tier: age >18 months, or public symbol removed without prior deprecation.
deprecated_never_removed.packet: Deprecation commit, replacement, dated callers, removal commit.
deprecated_never_removed.question: What replaces it and why are callers still present?

rollback_unsafe_change.name: Destructive migration that makes rollback impossible
rollback_unsafe_change.label: Pattern
rollback_unsafe_change.pitfall: DROP/RENAME/NOT NULL with irreversible down breaks rollbacks and hidden readers.
rollback_unsafe_change.signal: Migration with destructive DDL or absent/irreversible down; rank by same-commit app edits to name-matching column, table-qualified string references at HEAD, later fix/revert on table.
rollback_unsafe_change.packet: Up/down bodies, remaining references, later fixes.
rollback_unsafe_change.question: Can the previous release run on migrated schema?
rollback_unsafe_change.noise: Same-release tables, empty tables, DROP INDEX, ADD NULL.
rollback_unsafe_change.example: Column renamed with ORM change; nightly export selects dropped column.

exception_message_matching_consumer.name: Error message edited while consumers match the text
exception_message_matching_consumer.label: AntiPattern
exception_message_matching_consumer.pitfall: Callers match on message strings; rewording breaks them.
exception_message_matching_consumer.signal: Changed message literal in raise/throw/log; HEAD consumer (any file type, tests ranked lower) with shared >=12-char fragment matching old text only.
exception_message_matching_consumer.question: Is the consumer dead or broken?
exception_message_matching_consumer.noise: Short fragments, consumers matching both texts, third-party messages.

cascade_and_fk_rule_change.name: Foreign key delete/cascade rule changed
cascade_and_fk_rule_change.label: Pattern
cascade_and_fk_rule_change.pitfall: Cascade changes mass-delete or orphan children.
cascade_and_fk_rule_change.signal: Old vs new on ON DELETE/on_delete/dependent/cascade/orphanRemoval for same relationship; rank CASCADE additions and PROTECT/RESTRICT removals first; include other relationships of parent.
cascade_and_fk_rule_change.packet: Old/new lines, parent model, children rules.
cascade_and_fk_rule_change.question: What happens to child data on parent delete?
cascade_and_fk_rule_change.noise: Initial creation, test models, arg reorders.
cascade_and_fk_rule_change.example: on_delete CASCADE changed to PROTECT after purge removed history.

special_case_accretion.name: Function grown by successive special-case patches
special_case_accretion.label: Pattern
special_case_accretion.pitfall: Functions accrete branches per customer or edge case; each is a past incident.
special_case_accretion.signal: Tree-sitter branch-node counts per diary version; grew >=3x across >=8 modifying commits, >=50% net-adding, >=2 fix-class, none reducing by >=10%.
special_case_accretion.question: What incident does each branch represent?
special_case_accretion.noise: Skip dispatch tables, parsers, generated, tests, migrations.
special_case_accretion.example: calculate_shipping() grows from 12 to 240 lines with 31 country branches.

generated_code_hand_edited.name: Generated file edited by hand
generated_code_hand_edited.label: AntiPattern
generated_code_hand_edited.pitfall: Hand edits to generated files vanish on regeneration.
generated_code_hand_edited.why: Fixed bug comes back; marks generator limits.
generated_code_hand_edited.signal: Header regex at parent commit (do not edit|generated by|@generated) or generated names; commit touches it but none of its inputs (resolved via header or sibling basename), diff <40 lines or message fix/manual/patch; prioritise regen commits deleting earlier manual hunks.
generated_code_hand_edited.packet: Header, diffs, generator inputs, regen commits.
generated_code_hand_edited.question: Which edits must be reapplied at source?
generated_code_hand_edited.noise: Exclude lockfiles, snapshots, pure regeneration, bulk.
generated_code_hand_edited.example: Hand-patched rendered deployment.yaml overwritten by helm template.
sources: Winters et al., SWE at Google

https_scheme_redirect_flip.name: HTTPS redirect enforcement flipped or reverted
https_scheme_redirect_flip.label: RejectedAttempt
https_scheme_redirect_flip.pitfall: Redirects behind TLS-terminating proxies loop and get reverted.
https_scheme_redirect_flip.signal: Per-file key state tracking for SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT|force-ssl-redirect|redirect-to-https|UseHttpsRedirection: flip-flop within 15 commits, or flip followed by loop|redirect|healthcheck messages in next 10 commits; attach proxy-trust settings.
https_scheme_redirect_flip.question: What coupling between TLS, proto trust and probes?
https_scheme_redirect_flip.example: Enabled behind ALB without proxy header, reverted.

terraform_replace_forcing_change.name: IaC change that forces replacement
terraform_replace_forcing_change.label: AntiPattern
terraform_replace_forcing_change.pitfall: Renames without moved blocks or ForceNew edits destroy stateful resources.
terraform_replace_forcing_change.signal: Per commit, removed/added resource headers of same stateful type (allowlist) with no moved block/state mv/import; edits to identifier|cluster_identifier|bucket|engine|snapshot_identifier in stateful blocks; skip dev/ephemeral.
terraform_replace_forcing_change.question: Would apply destroy this?

iac_guardrail_removal.name: IaC safety guard removed or masked
iac_guardrail_removal.label: AntiPattern
iac_guardrail_removal.pitfall: prevent_destroy, deletion_protection, skip_final_snapshot flipped to unblock applies.
iac_guardrail_removal.signal: Guard flips protective->unprotective or new ignore_changes in non-dev paths; boost same resource renamed/removed within 3 commits or guard never restored at HEAD.
iac_guardrail_removal.question: Why lifted and was it restored?

satd_lingering_in_hot_code.name: Lingering TODO/FIXME/HACK in actively changing code
satd_lingering_in_hot_code.label: AntiPattern
satd_lingering_in_hot_code.pitfall: Self-admitted debt comments survive for years while the enclosing code keeps being edited and fixed.
satd_lingering_in_hot_code.why: A stated known limitation plus churn is a hidden constraint an editor should read first.
satd_lingering_in_hot_code.signal: Added-line SATD regex with >=30 chars naming a concrete limitation; still at HEAD; age >=180d, enclosing symbol modified >=5x (excluding bulk/format), >=1 fix-lineage commit after the comment. Rank fix count over modification count.
satd_lingering_in_hot_code.packet: Comment plus context, introducing commit, later commits on symbol, fix count, linked issue state.
satd_lingering_in_hot_code.question: What limitation does the comment describe and have later changes respected or worked around it?
satd_lingering_in_hot_code.noise: Skip vendored/generated, tests, docs, license headers, generic TODOs, symbol-less comments.
satd_lingering_in_hot_code.example: 'HACK: retry once because upstream drops first connection' survives 4 years with 9 edits.

lock_churn_concurrency_scars.name: Locks added, removed or narrowed around a symbol
lock_churn_concurrency_scars.label: Pattern
lock_churn_concurrency_scars.pitfall: Locks added for races are later removed for speed.
lock_churn_concurrency_scars.signal: Lock token added in a race-zone fix and later removed/narrowed, or >=3 lock-line edits per symbol; add co-modified lock-bearing symbols; exclude tests and lockfiles.
lock_churn_concurrency_scars.packet: Lock timeline, race fixes, call chain.
lock_churn_concurrency_scars.question: What state does the lock protect?
lock_churn_concurrency_scars.example: Lock removed in 'speed up cache path', re-added 3 weeks later.

persistent_state_mount_change.name: Persistent volume, mount or data path changed
persistent_state_mount_change.label: AntiPattern
persistent_state_mount_change.pitfall: Renaming a volume/PVC/data dir starts services on empty storage.
persistent_state_mount_change.signal: Removed/renamed named-volume key or claimName whose old name absent at HEAD; mountPath or data-dir env change on service with volume; skip tmpfs, emptyDir-only, dev/test/override files; suppress with migration script in commit.
persistent_state_mount_change.packet: Diff, services mounting it, migration scripts.
persistent_state_mount_change.question: Was data migrated?
persistent_state_mount_change.example: db_data renamed postgres_data; next up creates empty DB.

release_workflow_edit_fix_chain.name: Release/publish pipeline repaired repeatedly
release_workflow_edit_fix_chain.label: Pattern
release_workflow_edit_fix_chain.pitfall: Release workflows are debugged live; versions are immutable.
release_workflow_edit_fix_chain.signal: Release-file globs: >=3 fix-message commits to same file within 24h (primary); tag proximity as booster; flag deleted/re-pushed tags and version bump after chain; exclude bumps/bots.
release_workflow_edit_fix_chain.packet: Ordered cluster diffs, tags, step diffs.
release_workflow_edit_fix_chain.question: What must editors never change casually?
release_workflow_edit_fix_chain.example: Five workflow commits after v2.0.0 ends in v2.0.1.

k8s_availability_knob_reduction.name: Replicas, PDB, rollout strategy or topology reduced
k8s_availability_knob_reduction.label: AntiPattern
k8s_availability_knob_reduction.pitfall: Redundancy knobs are cut to save cost or unblock deploys.
k8s_availability_knob_reduction.signal: replicas/minReplicas to 1 or >=2x drop, deleted PodDisruptionBudget, removed anti-affinity/topologySpread in prod paths, no HPA added in same commit; boost incident/cost/drain messages.
k8s_availability_knob_reduction.question: What guarantee was lost?
k8s_availability_knob_reduction.noise: Skip dev/staging/examples, HPA introductions, chart refactors.
k8s_availability_knob_reduction.example: PDB deleted to unblock drain, never restored.

retry_without_backoff_jitter.name: Retry added without backoff, jitter or cap
retry_without_backoff_jitter.label: AntiPattern
retry_without_backoff_jitter.pitfall: Naive retries synchronise clients and multiply load on a degraded dependency.
retry_without_backoff_jitter.why: Fix versus seed of a retry storm.
retry_without_backoff_jitter.signal: Commit adds retry construct (tenacity, backoff, loop with sleep) in symbol calling network/queue client; post-commit body lacks backoff/jitter/cap; require fix commit or later backoff added to same symbol.
retry_without_backoff_jitter.packet: Intro diff, body, callee, later retry commits.
retry_without_backoff_jitter.question: Is the retry bounded, jittered, idempotent?
retry_without_backoff_jitter.noise: Skip tests, scripts, CI polling, local locks.
retry_without_backoff_jitter.example: Retry in 'fix flaky checkout' with fixed 1s sleep x10.

revert_of_revert_or_reapplied_change.name: Reverted change re-landed with modification
revert_of_revert_or_reapplied_change.label: RejectedAttempt
revert_of_revert_or_reapplied_change.pitfall: A reverted change lands again altered; the delta encodes the first attempt's flaw.
revert_of_revert_or_reapplied_change.signal: Revert R of C; C2 within ~90 days linked by Reland/Reapply subject, patch-id similarity or >=50% overlap/shared symbols; non-whitespace delta >=3 lines.
revert_of_revert_or_reapplied_change.packet: C, R, C2 diffs and diff-of-diffs.
revert_of_revert_or_reapplied_change.question: What changed between failed and successful versions?
revert_of_revert_or_reapplied_change.noise: Exclude identical cherry-picks, whitespace deltas, bumps.

pii_in_log_statement_fix.name: Sensitive data scrubbed from logs, siblings remain
pii_in_log_statement_fix.label: Pattern
pii_in_log_statement_fix.pitfall: One-site log scrubs leave siblings logging secrets.
pii_in_log_statement_fix.signal: Scrub commit (message redact|mask|scrub or diff removing password/token/authorization identifiers from log calls); HEAD scan of log calls interpolating same identifiers or whole request/headers/payload objects.
pii_in_log_statement_fix.packet: Scrub diff, sibling log lines, redaction helper.
pii_in_log_statement_fix.question: Which sibling sites bypass the helper?
pii_in_log_statement_fix.example: Authorization masked in HTTP client; retry module logs headers.

swallow_introduced_masks_later_fix.name: Swallowed error or suppressed script failure later unmasked
swallow_introduced_masks_later_fix.label: AntiPattern
swallow_introduced_masks_later_fix.pitfall: Empty catch, except: pass, || true, set +e, continue-on-error hide a failure revealed later.
swallow_introduced_masks_later_fix.why: Failures at this site must propagate; pipelines report success falsely.
swallow_introduced_masks_later_fix.signal: Added swallow in code (empty/pass/continue handlers, enclosing symbol) or scripts/Make/workflow run blocks (|| true, set +e, 2>/dev/null, --force, -auto-approve); pair only with later fix-classified commit within 90-365 days touching same symbol/nearby lines or removing it; require message/diff referencing error.
swallow_introduced_masks_later_fix.packet: Intro hunk, fix diff, days between, callers.
swallow_introduced_masks_later_fix.question: What fault did the swallow conceal?
swallow_introduced_masks_later_fix.noise: Tests, cleanup/trap, grep/rm -f idioms, optional-lookup except ImportError.
swallow_introduced_masks_later_fix.example: kubectl apply || true hides a manifest error.

tls_hsts_policy_ratchet.name: TLS min-version / cipher / HSTS change
tls_hsts_policy_ratchet.label: AntiPattern
tls_hsts_policy_ratchet.pitfall: HSTS preload/includeSubDomains is a one-way ratchet; TLS floor changes cut clients.
tls_hsts_policy_ratchet.signal: Numeric parse on HSTS lines/SECURE_HSTS_* (max-age only there): >=10x raise, includeSubDomains/preload added, TLS floor lowered, or increase reverted within 30 commits.
tls_hsts_policy_ratchet.question: Which direction is irreversible?
tls_hsts_policy_ratchet.noise: Test certs, dev nginx, vendored images.

wip_trial_and_error_sequence.name: Trial-and-error commit sequence on one hunk or value
wip_trial_and_error_sequence.label: RejectedAttempt
wip_trial_and_error_sequence.pitfall: Oscillating edits to the same lines record unresolved diagnosis.
wip_trial_and_error_sequence.signal: Within 7 days/one branch, >=3 commits (2 for CI/Dockerfile/infra) with overlapping hunk ranges and A->B->A hash return or >=2 try/again/still-fail messages; rank by oscillations.
wip_trial_and_error_sequence.packet: Ordered hunk diffs, messages, final state.
wip_trial_and_error_sequence.question: What was tried and why did each fail?
wip_trial_and_error_sequence.noise: Exclude lockfiles, version bumps, whitespace flips, merges.
wip_trial_and_error_sequence.example: CI workflow edited six times in an hour ends pinning the runner image.
sources: Hindle et al., MSR 2008 (weak; find CI-churn studies)

missing_cochange_partner.name: Usual co-change partner missed, fixed in a follow-up
missing_cochange_partner.label: Pattern
missing_cochange_partner.pitfall: Files that nearly always change together are sometimes changed alone and fixed later.
missing_cochange_partner.why: Yields 'when A changes update B' rules with proof.
missing_cochange_partner.signal: Rule A=>B confidence >=0.8, support >=5; >=2 violations (A without B, then B without A by same author within 14 days); message words only boost; exclude generated B/lockfiles.
missing_cochange_partner.question: Why must B change with A?
missing_cochange_partner.noise: Drop test/subject, docs, changelog, explicit-link pairs.
missing_cochange_partner.example: Eclipse change needs plug-in manifest edit; omission breaks runtime.

vendored_copy_local_patch.name: Vendored third-party code with local modifications
vendored_copy_local_patch.label: Pattern
vendored_copy_local_patch.pitfall: Copied libraries stop receiving upstream fixes and lose local patches on refresh.
vendored_copy_local_patch.why: Refresh loses fixes; missing upstream security fixes.
vendored_copy_local_patch.signal: Vendor-like dir (vendor|third_party|ext|deps) with bulk first commit, >=2 later non-bulk commits; rank by re-vendor commit deleting lines earlier local commits added. Exclude manifest-managed dirs.
vendored_copy_local_patch.packet: Import commit, local diffs, update commits.
vendored_copy_local_patch.question: Which patches must survive upgrade?
vendored_copy_local_patch.noise: Skip go mod vendor, node_modules, minified, pure re-vendors.
vendored_copy_local_patch.example: vendor/tinyxml has 3 local buffer fixes, upstream 2 majors ahead.

version_literal_multifile_sync_lag.name: Version literal bumped in some files, repaired later
version_literal_multifile_sync_lag.label: Pattern
version_literal_multifile_sync_lag.pitfall: Release versions in many files; bumps miss some.
version_literal_multifile_sync_lag.signal: Semver X->Y literal changes in version-field contexts (version=, __version__, ARG VERSION, appVersion) across files; recurring version file set over >=2 releases; emit when release covers strict subset or follow-up repairs rest; exclude deps/lockfiles.
version_literal_multifile_sync_lag.packet: Release commits, file sets, repair commits, release tool config.
version_literal_multifile_sync_lag.question: Which files must be bumped together?

migration_on_boot_placement_change.name: Where DB migrations run changed
migration_on_boot_placement_change.label: Pattern
migration_on_boot_placement_change.pitfall: Entrypoint migrations race at scale; moving changes failure semantics.
migration_on_boot_placement_change.signal: Migration command moves between deploy surfaces (entrypoint, hook, initContainer, Job, CI step) in scoped files, or lock/wait-for-db fix within ~20 commits.
migration_on_boot_placement_change.packet: Placement before/after, replicas, hooks, lock fixes.
migration_on_boot_placement_change.question: What concurrency assumptions must new migrations meet?
migration_on_boot_placement_change.example: alembic moved to entrypoint; 12 replicas deadlock.

dependency_adopt_then_remove.name: Library added then removed or replaced
dependency_adopt_then_remove.label: RejectedAttempt
dependency_adopt_then_remove.pitfall: Trialed libraries are dropped for unrecorded reasons and re-proposed.
dependency_adopt_then_remove.why: Assistant would re-suggest the rejected library.
dependency_adopt_then_remove.signal: Manifest add/remove events per normalised package: add then remove within <=180 days/<=200 commits (or >=2 cycles) or removed with replacement Q; require explanatory message or import of P between; gather conflict|alpine|license|vulnerab messages.
dependency_adopt_then_remove.packet: Add/remove diffs, usage diffs, messages, replacement.
dependency_adopt_then_remove.question: Why was P abandoned?
dependency_adopt_then_remove.noise: Dev tools, renames, squash churn, bots.
dependency_adopt_then_remove.example: python-magic removed after libmagic failed on Windows.

k8s_resource_limit_churn.name: Container resource limits and runtime memory/CPU settings out of step
k8s_resource_limit_churn.label: Pattern
k8s_resource_limit_churn.pitfall: Limits and runtime flags (-Xmx, GOMEMLIMIT, workers) tuned independently cause OOMKills or throttling.
k8s_resource_limit_churn.signal: Parseable YAML/HCL changes on prod-looking paths: memory >=1.5x, limit removal, request/limit equality change, >=3 changes in 365 days, heap/limit ratio >0.85, worker count > CPU limit, OOM/137/throttl fix messages; include autoscaler params; list nearby commits only.
k8s_resource_limit_churn.packet: Value timeline, runtime flags, OOM messages, sibling services.
k8s_resource_limit_churn.question: What sets the floor and which code changes need coordinated bumps?
k8s_resource_limit_churn.noise: Skip dev overlays, single definitions, VPA bots.
k8s_resource_limit_churn.example: 512Mi to 2Gi after OOMKills caused by an unbounded cache.

probe_and_healthcheck_drift.name: Liveness/readiness/startup probe or health handler changes
probe_and_healthcheck_drift.label: Pattern
probe_and_healthcheck_drift.pitfall: Probes checking dependencies or tight thresholds cause restart storms.
probe_and_healthcheck_drift.why: A dependency blip becomes fleet restarts.
probe_and_healthcheck_drift.signal: Config-first: probe/HEALTHCHECK diffs with >=2 value changes, removal, threshold<=1, timeout<=1s, liveness path == readiness; attach handler body and callees when path maps to a parsed symbol; boost CrashLoop messages.
probe_and_healthcheck_drift.packet: Probe timeline, handler body, startup changes.
probe_and_healthcheck_drift.question: What must the handler never depend on?
probe_and_healthcheck_drift.example: /healthz queries Postgres as livenessProbe; failover restarts all pods.

serialization_field_renumber.name: Protobuf/Thrift/Avro field number or type change
serialization_field_renumber.label: Pattern
serialization_field_renumber.pitfall: Reusing tags or retyping fields corrupts data in mixed-version fleets.
serialization_field_renumber.signal: .proto/.thrift/.avsc only: tag reuse, removal without reserved, type change on same number, enum value removal, added required; exclude generated dirs, new messages. Version constants as separate lower kind.
serialization_field_renumber.packet: Message before/after, history of number, consumers.
serialization_field_renumber.question: Was wire compat broken?
serialization_field_renumber.noise: Alpha packages, comment edits, additive optionals.

crap_hotspot.name: CRAP x churn hotspot
crap_hotspot.label: AntiPattern
crap_hotspot.pitfall: Chasing a global coverage percentage instead of testing the few complex, frequently changed functions where a regression is likely.
crap_hotspot.why: CRAP (comp^2*(1-cov)^3+comp) flags complex code with poor coverage; Tornhill and Nagappan & Ball show churn x complexity locates code that actually breaks; Google found developers want guidance on which uncovered lines matter. Oracle's binary test_gap cannot separate 0% from 90% covered.
crap_hotspot.signal: Emit only with a measured-coverage CRAP, or, without coverage, use a labelled 'unmeasured' tier: cc>=10 AND fixes>=2 AND no static test call link (not name match). Require churn percentile>=75 within non-bulk, non-rename commits and body >=20 lines. Drop the 'not meaningful' bucket from the main queue and sample it at 5% for calibration only. Collapse symbols already emitted by fix-prone-symbol-no-test into one packet.
crap_hotspot.packet: Function body with branch list; CRAP inputs; per-line coverage or 'no test link'; last 10 commits (message, date, author); fix-lineage rows and guards; linked tests with weights; callers.
crap_hotspot.question: Which branches carry the complexity and are uncovered, and which historical bugs would a test for them have caught? Name the 2-5 test cases (input -> expected). Or say the churn is cosmetic, or the function is too tangled and should be split first.
crap_hotspot.noise: Drop bulk and rename-only churn; flat dispatch tables or constant elif chains; generated, vendored, migration, config files; single initial-commit churn; functions unchanged 2 years with no fixes.
crap_hotspot.example: parse_headers() cc=14, 20% covered, 9 commits in 6 months, 3 fixes; uncovered lines are the malformed-continuation branch both fixes changed. A test feeding an obs-fold header would have caught them.
sources: Tornhill, Your Code as a Crime Scene, 2015
Nagappan & Ball, Relative code churn measures, ICSE 2005
Ivankovic et al., Code Coverage at Google, FSE 2019

dead_config_key.name: Config option with no remaining consumer
dead_config_key.label: AntiPattern
dead_config_key.pitfall: Knobs remain after the code reading them is deleted, giving a false sense of control.
dead_config_key.why: A limit may have been silently dropped.
dead_config_key.signal: Key in config files with zero consumer literal at HEAD (normalised case/separators), which once had an in-repo consumer; commit removing last consumer did not touch the config. Limit-like or project-prefixed names only; suppress dynamic-lookup prefixes.
dead_config_key.packet: Orphan key, definitions, removal diff, neighbouring keys.
dead_config_key.question: Was the limit moved or silently dropped?
dead_config_key.noise: Skip framework-consumed keys, docs/examples, dynamic key construction.
dead_config_key.example: REQUEST_MAX_BYTES stays in values.yaml after the enforcing middleware is deleted.

removed_guard_then_regression.name: Defensive guard removed in refactor, then re-added by a fix
removed_guard_then_regression.label: RejectedAttempt
removed_guard_then_regression.pitfall: A fix-added guard looks like clutter; a refactor removes it and the bug returns.
removed_guard_then_regression.why: Near-proof the lines encode a hidden requirement.
removed_guard_then_regression.signal: Strong form only: fix F adds lines L; later commit R removes lines >=0.8 similar in same symbol/file; later fix F2 re-adds similar lines within 365 days.
removed_guard_then_regression.packet: F, R, F2 diffs and messages, diary, tests.
removed_guard_then_regression.question: What failure does the guard prevent?
removed_guard_then_regression.noise: Drop if moved in same commit, whitespace/comment guards.
removed_guard_then_regression.example: Refactor drops timezone special case; fix restores it a month later.

skip_xfail_never_removed.name: Disabled tests that stayed disabled
skip_xfail_never_removed.label: AntiPattern
skip_xfail_never_removed.pitfall: skip/skipif/xfail/it.skip/xit/test.todo markers added with vague reasons and never revisited; the subject has no effective test though the test map counts it.
skip_xfail_never_removed.why: Skipped tests inflate test_gap=0; flaky tests are quarantined then forgotten (Luo 2014, Eck 2019, Micco); a skip citing a fixed issue is free coverage.
skip_xfail_never_removed.signal: Marker present at HEAD in a test symbol, added >90 days ago, subject risk>=50 or >=1 subject fix since. Exclude skipif with a platform or version condition, importorskip, and markers under 30 days. Boost for unconditional skip, a flaky/TODO reason, or a referenced issue that is closed. Report whether the skipped test is the only static link to its subject.
skip_xfail_never_removed.packet: Commit A diff/message; test body; reason; subject commits and fixes since; whether skipped test is the only static link; CI snippet; linked issue state.
skip_xfail_never_removed.question: Is the skip still justified or abandoned? Can it simply be re-enabled (fix landed), repaired, or deleted? What did it assert?
skip_xfail_never_removed.noise: Specific platform skipif or importorskip with equivalent coverage elsewhere; markers <30 days; test.todo backlog repos; slow markers run in a separate job; vendored tests.
skip_xfail_never_removed.example: test_unicode_path xfail(reason='#41') for 14 months; #41 closed by 8de1. Remove xfail.
sources: Luo et al., Flaky tests, FSE 2014
Micco, State of CI Testing at Google, 2017
Parry et al., Survey of Flaky Tests, TOSEM 2021

doc_identifier_orphan.name: Docs/runbooks naming identifiers that no longer exist
doc_identifier_orphan.label: AntiPattern
doc_identifier_orphan.pitfall: Docs keep names of deleted/renamed symbols and paths.
doc_identifier_orphan.why: Assistants and on-call follow false instructions.
doc_identifier_orphan.signal: Backticked path and symbol tokens (flags/env later) in README/docs/runbooks absent at HEAD but present at doc's last-edit commit with lineage record; rank orphans per doc, prioritise runbooks/README.
doc_identifier_orphan.packet: Doc snippet, deleting/renaming commit, doc last edit.
doc_identifier_orphan.question: Stale or loose usage; current equivalent?
doc_identifier_orphan.noise: CHANGELOG, superseded ADRs, external tool commands, archived docs.
doc_identifier_orphan.example: make restore-db renamed db-recover in runbook.

env_var_config_contract_break.name: Env var contract broken between code and deploy config
env_var_config_contract_break.label: Pattern
env_var_config_contract_break.pitfall: Code reads env vars deploy files must supply; renames break boot.
env_var_config_contract_break.signal: (a) commit adds/renames consumer with no producer file touched, followed within 30 commits/14 days by wiring or missing env|KeyError fix; (c) consumer with no producer/default when repo has producer files. Denylist platform vars.
env_var_config_contract_break.question: What is the procedure to add or rename this var?
env_var_config_contract_break.noise: Exclude PATH/HOME/CI/PORT, test vars, defaulted optionals.
env_var_config_contract_break.example: DATABASE_URL renamed in code; Helm still sets old name.

resource_leak_fix_lineage.name: File descriptor, socket and connection leak fix recurrence
resource_leak_fix_lineage.label: Pattern
resource_leak_fix_lineage.pitfall: Handles leak on error paths; same shape recurs.
resource_leak_fix_lineage.why: Failures appear hours later far from the cause.
resource_leak_fix_lineage.signal: >=2 leak-worded commits in same module, each diff adding with/finally/close/defer; show ulimit/pool config; HEAD unguarded-open scan Python/JS only, cap 5.
resource_leak_fix_lineage.packet: Fix diffs, unguarded siblings, limits config.
resource_leak_fix_lineage.question: Which acquisition pattern leaked?
resource_leak_fix_lineage.example: Third resp.Body.Close fix in another module.

non_code_dependency_gap.name: Fixes in config, data, fixtures and conftest that no test link covers
non_code_dependency_gap.label: AntiPattern
non_code_dependency_gap.pitfall: The map is built from code symbols and imports, so edits to SQL, templates, YAML/JSON config, fixtures, golden files and conftest.py select no tests.
non_code_dependency_gap.why: Ekstazi's finding is that file dependencies beyond classes (resources, config) must be tracked; many bugs live in migrations, feature flags and templates, so assess_change is silent on a whole class of edits.
non_code_dependency_gap.signal: Fix-commit (or non-bulk) edits to non-code resource files (sql, yml, yaml, json, toml, ini, html, templates/, migrations/, fixtures/, conftest.py) where tests_to_run is empty or below 0.3. Require at least one of: (a) a test file contains the file's basename or relative path as a string literal (strong, always emit), or (b) a test was edited in the same commit. Drop (c). Rank by the count of distinct fix commits touching the file. Exclude lockfiles, CI files, docs and snapshots, and comment-only or whitespace-only diffs. Cap at 2 per directory.
non_code_dependency_gap.packet: Diff of the non-code file; basename grep hits in tests and source; co-edited tests; current assess_change output; string-contract entries for its keys.
non_code_dependency_gap.question: Which tests would exercise the file, or is it untested configuration? What single test (parse and check required keys, or migrate forward and back)? Is the missing link a map rule gap?
non_code_dependency_gap.noise: Docs, README, lockfiles, CI-only files, .gitignore, comment-only changes; snapshot files (snapshot-rubber-stamp).
non_code_dependency_gap.example: 4 of 11 recent fixes touched config/limits.yaml; tests/test_limits.py loads it by path string but is not selected. Add a resource link and a test asserting every key is read by LimitConfig, since fix 7be1 renamed a key.
sources: Vasic et al., File-level vs. module-level regression test selection for .NET, FSE 2017

partial_api_migration_residue.name: Mechanical migration that left old-API call sites behind
partial_api_migration_residue.label: Pattern
partial_api_migration_residue.pitfall: A sweep commit leaves hard cases or regressions using the old form.
partial_api_migration_residue.why: Residue shows why sites could not migrate or are regressions.
partial_api_migration_residue.signal: Sweep commits with line-paired single-identifier substitutions old->new in >=10 hunks across >=3 files; count old token at HEAD non-test, split pre-sweep vs post-sweep additions; message keyword as boost; rank by post-sweep additions.
partial_api_migration_residue.packet: Sweep hunks, remaining occurrences with dates, post-sweep additions.
partial_api_migration_residue.question: Why were sites left; which form should new code use?
partial_api_migration_residue.noise: Skip short/common tokens, vendored, tests, docs.
partial_api_migration_residue.example: 'replace requests.get with http_client.get' leaves 11 sites, 4 added later.

route_and_middleware_order_change.name: Order-sensitive list reordered or inserted
route_and_middleware_order_change.label: Pattern
route_and_middleware_order_change.signal: Same normalised line removed and added within one block (list literal with >=3 entries) or equal removed/added multisets; neighbours include auth|cors|csrf|session|error; escalate on re-reorder within 15 commits or fix within 14 days.
route_and_middleware_order_change.question: What ordering invariant does it encode?
route_and_middleware_order_change.noise: Formatter re-sorts, import reorders, package.json sorting, bulk.
route_and_middleware_order_change.example: corsheaders moved above Auth; later sort breaks it.

test_added_at_fix_then_lost.name: Regression test from a fix later lost or detached
test_added_at_fix_then_lost.label: AntiPattern
test_added_at_fix_then_lost.pitfall: A regression test added with a fix is later deleted, skipped, renamed to something unrelated, or no longer reaches the guard.
test_added_at_fix_then_lost.why: The fate of fix-linked tests is the clearest measure of test erosion.
test_added_at_fix_then_lost.signal: For each fix commit with security/regression/race zones that added or changed a test symbol in the same commit: at HEAD the symbol is deleted, skip-marked, assertion count reduced, or has lost its static link to the fixed function, while the fixed function still exists. Drop the similarity search and rename-token logic for v1.
test_added_at_fix_then_lost.packet: Fix diff/message; r body at F; fate timeline; guard at HEAD; links; issue text.
test_added_at_fix_then_lost.question: Is the original bug still guarded by an equivalent test? If not, show the original test adapted to the current API with the bug-encoding assertion.
test_added_at_fix_then_lost.noise: Equivalent test exists (similarity>=0.8); guarded function deleted; fixes older than a major rewrite.
test_added_at_fix_then_lost.example: Fix 9f3 added test_cart_empty; later renamed test_cart_2 with the assert removed while 'if not items' remains.
sources: Understanding Test Deletion in Java Applications, MSR 2025

hard_to_test_risky_code.name: Risky uncovered code needing a seam
hard_to_test_risky_code.label: AntiPattern
hard_to_test_risky_code.pitfall: Writing brittle e2e tests, or giving up, on risky functions mixing logic with I/O, globals, subprocess or time.
hard_to_test_risky_code.why: Seams and characterization tests are the route into legacy code (Feathers); developers skip hard-to-test code (Beller 2015).
hard_to_test_risky_code.signal: Symbol with no static test link and no test reachable via the call graph, >=2 fix commits (or CRAP>=30), and >=1 I/O-like call. Rank by fixes times branch count. Exclude thin wrappers (<=5 statements with one I/O call), non-imported scripts and CLI mains, and symbols with a characterization test. Include fix diffs as the source of test inputs. Also surface the same untested+risky list without an I/O requirement as a plain 'risky untested' variant.
hard_to_test_risky_code.packet: Body annotated with I/O lines; branch dependency; callers; fixtures nearby; fix history.
hard_to_test_risky_code.question: Which pure decision logic can be extracted and tested via a table? What is the characterization test (inputs from fix diffs)? Cost vs value, or not worth it.
hard_to_test_risky_code.noise: Thin I/O wrappers; non-imported scripts/CLIs; existing characterization tests.
hard_to_test_risky_code.example: sync_repo reads env, shells out to git, then selects branches; the pure selection rule (fixed twice) can be extracted.
sources: Feathers, Working Effectively with Legacy Code, 2004

monkeypatch_dependency_bump_overlap.name: Runtime monkeypatch and later dependency bumps
monkeypatch_dependency_bump_overlap.label: AntiPattern
monkeypatch_dependency_bump_overlap.pitfall: Patches of third-party internals go stale after upgrades.
monkeypatch_dependency_bump_overlap.why: Bumps silently neutralise or break patches.
monkeypatch_dependency_bump_overlap.signal: Attribute assignment on imported module resolving (with alias table) to manifest package; >=1 lockfile version change after the last edit of the patch; rank by bump count.
monkeypatch_dependency_bump_overlap.question: Is the patch still needed?
monkeypatch_dependency_bump_overlap.noise: Tests, mocks, documented bootstrap, patches edited after latest bump.
monkeypatch_dependency_bump_overlap.example: HTTPAdapter.send wrapped in 2021; requests bumped twice.

szz_bug_introducing_commit.name: SZZ bug-introducing commit for a fix
szz_bug_introducing_commit.label: AntiPattern
szz_bug_introducing_commit.pitfall: Blame of a fix's removed lines gives the risky change and defect lifetime.
szz_bug_introducing_commit.why: Reveals the violated invariant and test gap; shared infrastructure.
szz_bug_introducing_commit.signal: Fixes in security/race/regression/performance zones; blame -w -M -C on parent; single origin explaining >=50% of lines and lifetime >=14 days; skip bulk/rename/format/move origins.
szz_bug_introducing_commit.packet: Fix and introducer diffs, lifetime, intermediate commits.
szz_bug_introducing_commit.question: What assumption did the introducing change get wrong?
szz_bug_introducing_commit.example: Null-check removed in a refactor blamed by an NPE fix 6 months later.

seam_mocked_only.name: Seam only ever tested with the callee mocked
seam_mocked_only.label: AntiPattern
seam_mocked_only.pitfall: Every test of a caller replaces its cross-package callee with patch, stub or MagicMock, and no test anywhere runs the real callee through that caller, so unit coverage is high but the seam has zero real exercise.
seam_mocked_only.why: Mocks encode only the author's belief about the callee; Spadini et al. found mocked internals correlate with brittle tests and mocks target external or hard-to-test dependencies. Here the subject is fine and the hidden part is the other side of the seam.
seam_mocked_only.signal: For each first-party symbol E patched in tests, check whether any test linked to E or its callers imports and calls E without patching it; flag when none does, E is not I/O/clock/subprocess/network, and E has >=1 fix or fan_in>=2. Include patch lines with return_value literals in the packet.
seam_mocked_only.packet: Edge; caller body; patch lines with mocked return values; E's real return/raise sites and shape comparison; E fix history; E's own-package tests.
seam_mocked_only.question: Do the mocked values match what E really returns including errors? If E is deterministic and cheap, replace one patch with the real callee and state the assertion; if I/O or slow, add a contract test of E's real output against the mocked shape.
seam_mocked_only.noise: Skip network, filesystem, clock, random, subprocess targets; client/adapters packages; mocks with autospec when a real test exists elsewhere.
seam_mocked_only.example: report.build() is tested only with a patched store.query() returning tuples, but the real store returns sqlite Row objects and the dashboard broke. Add one test with a real in-memory store.
sources: Spadini, Aniche, Bruntink and Bacchelli, To mock or not to mock?, MSR 2017
Winters et al., ch.13 Test Doubles

process_seam_mocked.name: Subprocess, CLI and stdio boundaries only tested with mocks
process_seam_mocked.label: AntiPattern
process_seam_mocked.pitfall: One package invokes another (or the repo's own CLI/MCP server, git) via subprocess, stdio or sockets and tests patch subprocess.run or the transport, so encoding, quoting, env, stdin and exit codes never cross the real boundary.
process_seam_mocked.why: Process boundaries carry platform behaviour (Windows quoting, console encodings, handle inheritance) that mocks cannot reproduce and are historically bug-dense; Oracle's own MCP hang fix (e220ae2) is the example.
process_seam_mocked.signal: Non-test call sites of subprocess.run/Popen/check_output/check_call, os.system, asyncio.create_subprocess_*, child_process.spawn/exec/execFile. Flag when (a) every test mapped to the enclosing function patches that call (mock.patch targeting subprocess.* or the wrapper) and no test runs it unmocked, and (b) the enclosing file or function has >=1 fix commit or a message matching stdin|encoding|timeout|hang|quote|shell|windows|utf. Rank by fix count, then by the call site being reachable from a public entry point. Exclude one-off scripts and tools under build/ or scripts/.
process_seam_mocked.packet: Call site and argv construction; tests with patches and fake output; fix commits; nearby platform branches.
process_seam_mocked.question: Which real failure modes (non-ASCII path, spaces, Windows, closed stdin, non-zero exit) occurred or could occur? Specify a test running a trivial real child with a timeout asserting exit code, stdout decoding, no hang.
process_seam_mocked.noise: External tools not installed in CI by design (git is fine); one-off build scripts; calls already covered by an unmocked test with timeout.
process_seam_mocked.example: The MCP hang on Windows (e220ae2) was fixed by passing empty stdin to every subprocess; all git wrapper tests patch subprocess.run. Add a real child with stdin closed under a timeout.
sources: Winters et al., ch.13-14 (hermetic and larger tests)
Python docs, subprocess security considerations and Windows helpers

ci_test_disabled.name: Tests disabled or narrowed in CI config
ci_test_disabled.label: AntiPattern
ci_test_disabled.pitfall: CI edits comment out tests, add continue-on-error, narrow paths/--ignore/-k/--deselect, drop matrix entries or coverage upload.
ci_test_disabled.why: CI protects only when gating (Hilton 2016; Vasilescu 2015); test selection must not silently shrink (Micco).
ci_test_disabled.signal: Scan diffs of .github/workflows/*, tox.ini, pytest.ini, pyproject [tool.pytest*], jest and vitest config and Makefile test targets. Match added lines with continue-on-error: true, allow_failure, if: false, '--ignore', '--deselect', '-k "not', testPathIgnorePatterns, paths-ignore, matrix exclude, '--maxfail', or a commented-out test command. Also match removed lines containing a test command or coverage upload. Resolve excluded paths against the test map. Add a bonus if the exclusion is still present at HEAD and fix commits touched the excluded area afterwards. Drop docs-only path filters and matrix additions.
ci_test_disabled.packet: CI diff and message; excluded tests/modules and risk; fixes in excluded area after; matrix before/after; discussion.
ci_test_disabled.question: Justified temporary quarantine (still temporary?) or permanent silent loss? Minimal restoration (re-enable job, mark single tests)?
ci_test_disabled.noise: Docs-only path filters; announced EOL runtime drops; matrix additions; nightly slow splits with equivalent coverage.
ci_test_disabled.example: --ignore=tests/integration added in 'unblock release', never reverted; 3 later db/ fixes were integration-only.
sources: Micco, State of CI Testing at Google, 2017

timeout_added_after_hang_siblings_unboun.name: Timeout added after a hang, siblings still unbounded
timeout_added_after_hang_siblings_unboun.label: AntiPattern
timeout_added_after_hang_siblings_unboun.pitfall: One call gets a timeout; same-client siblings stay unbounded.
timeout_added_after_hang_siblings_unboun.signal: Fix (hang|stuck|deadlock|timeout message) adding timeout= to known HTTP/DB client call; >=2 non-test siblings at HEAD of same callee without timeout and no session default; Python/JS/TS.
timeout_added_after_hang_siblings_unboun.packet: Fix diff, sibling sites, library default.
timeout_added_after_hang_siblings_unboun.question: Which siblings share the risk?

weakened_assertion.name: Assertion weakened or removed in an edit
weakened_assertion.label: AntiPattern
weakened_assertion.pitfall: An existing test is edited to assert less (assertEqual to assertTrue, approx tolerance widened, asserts removed, raises(Specific) to raises(Exception)).
weakened_assertion.why: Weakening makes a failing test green without fixing code, while coverage is unchanged (Pinto 2012; Petrovic 2018).
weakened_assertion.signal: Commit touches a test file and the hunks show net removed assertion lines (assert/expect/assertEqual) with fewer added, OR a strict-to-loose swap on the same line (assertEqual to assertTrue, ==value to >0, raises(Specific) to raises(Exception)), OR a tolerance literal increase (approx/rel/abs/delta). Require the same commit to modify a non-test file or the message to match fix|flaky|ci|broken. Exclude bulk commits, commits that add at least as many assertions as they remove, and renames. Use hunk regexes, not AST, in the first version.
weakened_assertion.packet: Before/after test with assertion diff; subject diff in same commit; message; strength delta; later fixes; other stronger tests.
weakened_assertion.question: Did behaviour legitimately become less deterministic, or was a failing assertion muted? State the strongest assertion to keep.
weakened_assertion.noise: Formatting and framework-migration rewrites; assertions split into multiple tests; tightened tolerances; bulk commits.
weakened_assertion.example: assertEqual(price(cart), 41.97) became assertTrue(price(cart) > 0) in the commit that changed rounding.

listen_address_scope_flip.name: Bind address / published port scope flipped
listen_address_scope_flip.label: AntiPattern
listen_address_scope_flip.pitfall: localhost vs 0.0.0.0 or unprefixed compose ports change exposure.
listen_address_scope_flip.signal: Server-start contexts only (CMD, command:, listen/serve/run, --host/--bind) flipped either direction; newly added unprefixed ports: entry for datastore image (postgres, redis, mongo, ...); generic host: keys excluded.
listen_address_scope_flip.packet: Line change, service type, commit message.
listen_address_scope_flip.question: What exposure does it create?
listen_address_scope_flip.noise: Dev compose for exposure rule, docs.

fix_recurrence_despite_existing_test.name: Bug recurred though a test already existed
fix_recurrence_despite_existing_test.label: AntiPattern
fix_recurrence_despite_existing_test.pitfall: A function with mapped, passing tests is fixed again; tests are weak rather than missing, so adding more tests is the wrong response.
fix_recurrence_despite_existing_test.why: Separates 'no test' from 'test that cannot fail'. Mutants are coupled to real faults, so survivors point at the weak assertion.
fix_recurrence_despite_existing_test.signal: Require a static-call (or measured) test link into S at F's parent, restricted to commits where the test file existed >14 days before F. Require a prior fix on S, and F not touching any test file in +-7 days. Exclude feature-like fixes (fix commit adding >40 production lines) and dependency bumps. Where afd-oracle mutate results exist for S, attach surviving mutants on F's lines and boost; without them mark 'unconfirmed'.
fix_recurrence_despite_existing_test.packet: Fix diff; test bodies at parent with assertion lists; prior fix; mutation results; difference between behaviour changed and behaviour asserted.
fix_recurrence_despite_existing_test.question: Which assertion should have failed and did not? Is the test asserting a return value or just no-raise? Give the strengthened assertion or added case.
fix_recurrence_despite_existing_test.noise: Name-match-only links with no call into S; feature changes disguised as fixes; dependency bump fixes.
fix_recurrence_despite_existing_test.example: price() fixed in 2e3a for rounding; test_price asserts result > 0. Assert exact Decimal for 3 inputs.
sources: Petrovic et al., Does mutation testing improve testing practices?, ICSE 2021
