security_header_csp_policy_change.name: CSP / security-header policy edited
security_header_csp_policy_change.label: AntiPattern
security_header_csp_policy_change.pitfall: CSP allowlists accumulate hosts and unsafe-*; tightening breaks embeds.
security_header_csp_policy_change.signal: unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval added, Report-Only to enforcing, wildcard added, or >=5 host additions per directive across commits (collapse same-commit); skip dev-server CSP.
security_header_csp_policy_change.question: Which need forced each exception?
security_header_csp_policy_change.example: script-src gains CDN and 'unsafe-eval' over six commits.
sources: Weichselbaum et al., CSP Is Dead

time_dependent_code_no_frozen_clock.name: Clock, timezone and locale code without controlled-clock tests
time_dependent_code_no_frozen_clock.label: AntiPattern
time_dependent_code_no_frozen_clock.pitfall: Functions read wall clock/timezone/locale, and tests avoid time assertions or depend on the real clock, sleeps or random seeds.
time_dependent_code_no_frozen_clock.why: Timezone mistakes dominate Python date/time bugs, mostly in single functions (MSR 2025); real-clock tests are Sleepy/Mystery Guest smells and flaky causes (Luo 2014).
time_dependent_code_no_frozen_clock.signal: Select symbols whose body calls datetime.now/utcnow/today, time.time, fromtimestamp, strptime/strftime, timedelta arithmetic, zoneinfo/pytz, Date.now or new Date, excluding logging-only use and perf_counter. Require at least one fix commit on the symbol whose message or diff matches date|time|tz|timezone|dst|utc|epoch, and require that no mapped test file imports freezegun, time_machine, jest fake timers or passes a clock parameter. Test-side hermeticity (unseeded random, real network) is a separate lower-value class, so leave it out.
time_dependent_code_no_frozen_clock.packet: Function with time calls; time-fix messages; test date literals and now() comparisons; callers comparing or storing results.
time_dependent_code_no_frozen_clock.question: Which exact dates break it (DST, month end, leap day, offsets)? Inject or patch the clock? Is stored time naive or aware? Give timestamps.
time_dependent_code_no_frozen_clock.noise: Logging, perf_counter timing, second-granularity rate limits, benchmarks; opaque ISO strings; e2e/integration/benchmark tests; sleeps <10 ms; fixtures freezing time.
time_dependent_code_no_frozen_clock.example: is_stale compares utcnow() to a local stamp, fixed once for DST; freeze at 2024-03-10 01:59 US/Eastern.
sources: It's About Time: Date and Time Bugs in Open Source Python, MSR 2025

comment_reference_decay.name: Comments pointing to moved, deleted or closed targets
comment_reference_decay.label: AntiPattern
comment_reference_decay.pitfall: 'see foo.py' links decay as code moves.
comment_reference_decay.why: Reference identifies the real coupling or obsolete workaround.
comment_reference_decay.signal: see/same as/copied from/defined in reference to path/symbol that lineage shows deleted or renamed; secondary: 'line N' in edited file, or closed issue with commented code unchanged.
comment_reference_decay.question: Where is the knowledge now?
comment_reference_decay.noise: External URLs, license, tests, generated docs.

boundary_fix_no_boundary_test.name: Comparison or constant changed by fix, boundary not pinned
boundary_fix_no_boundary_test.label: AntiPattern
boundary_fix_no_boundary_test.pitfall: A fix moves a comparison operator, +-1, limit or slice bound but tests only use interior values.
boundary_fix_no_boundary_test.why: Boundary-value analysis is the oldest evidence-backed technique; relational-operator and constant mutants survive most often; mutants couple to real faults (Just 2014); off-by-one studies (Sellik 2021). A fix proves the boundary was wrong once.
boundary_fix_no_boundary_test.signal: Fix-zone commit hunk in non-test code where old and new differ only in a relational operator (<,<=,>,>=,==,!=), an integer literal by +-1, or a slice/range bound. Exclude semantic no-ops, log/timeout/retry/version constants, and test files. Gate on: the fix commit itself did not add or edit a test that mentions the symbol, or the symbol has <=2 linked tests. Put the test literals and any flip-comparison mutation survivors in the packet as evidence for the analyst, not as gates.
boundary_fix_no_boundary_test.packet: Before/after hunk; function body; test argument literals; surviving mutants; commit message/issue.
boundary_fix_no_boundary_test.question: What are n-1, n, n+1 and expected outputs? Which are covered? Is the boundary a business rule (limits, pagination, dates) or an arbitrary internal bound? Give the parametrized test.
boundary_fix_no_boundary_test.noise: Log/UI/timeout/retry constants, version numbers, float epsilon contracts, len()-derived loop bounds, hunks in tests, semantic no-ops (x>=1 to x>0 on ints), property-based tests already hitting the boundary, symbols with zero tests (covered by fix-without-regression-test).
boundary_fix_no_boundary_test.example: 'if len(batch) > limit' fixed to '>=' ; no test uses exactly limit items. Test limit-1, limit, limit+1.
sources: Jeng & Weyuker, A Simplified Domain-Testing Strategy, TOSEM 1994
Ammann & Offutt, Introduction to Software Testing 2nd ed.
Myers, The Art of Software Testing, 1979
Sellik et al., Learning Off-By-One Mistakes, MSR 2021

build_flag_toggle_churn.name: Compiler or build flags flipped and reverted
build_flag_toggle_churn.label: Pattern
build_flag_toggle_churn.pitfall: -Werror, -O, sanitizer and strict toggles hide toolchain constraints.
build_flag_toggle_churn.signal: Flag token in build/config file diffs added then removed (or inverse) within 180 days, or removed with crash|miscompile|segfault|flaky|slow|UB message; skip comments and version bumps.
build_flag_toggle_churn.question: What toolchain problem made the flag necessary?
build_flag_toggle_churn.example: -O2 reduced to -O1 for one TU because gcc miscompiles.

concurrency_code_without_concurrent_test.name: Concurrency primitives with only sequential tests
concurrency_code_without_concurrent_test.label: AntiPattern
concurrency_code_without_concurrent_test.pitfall: Code using threads, locks, async tasks or shared mutable state is tested by one sequential caller.
concurrency_code_without_concurrent_test.why: 92% of concurrency bugs need an ordering among <=4 accesses, so a small targeted interleaving test exposes most (Lu 2008); race fixes and findings already exist.
concurrency_code_without_concurrent_test.signal: Select symbols with a race-zone fix or a concurrency safety finding, or with shared mutable state written under a Lock, Event or queue, whose mapped tests contain none of Thread, Barrier, gather, create_task, ThreadPoolExecutor, multiprocessing, Promise.all or asyncio concurrent constructs. Rank by race fixes x callers. Skip sequential-await asyncio, single-thread CLI locks, subprocess drain threads and test fixtures.
concurrency_code_without_concurrent_test.packet: Bodies with acquire/release and shared fields; race findings and fix diffs; tests lacking concurrency; critical operation order.
concurrency_code_without_concurrent_test.question: Name the interleaving and broken invariant; can a Barrier or injected hook force it deterministically? If single-threaded in practice, no test needed.
concurrency_code_without_concurrent_test.noise: Sequential-await asyncio; single-thread CLI locks; subprocess drain threads in one-off tools; test fixtures.
concurrency_code_without_concurrent_test.example: Cache.get_or_create does check-then-set unlocked, had a race fix, tested once; two-thread Barrier test.
sources: Lu et al., Learning from Mistakes, ASPLOS 2008

config_change_fix_chain.name: Config/IaC change followed by a fix to the same key
config_change_fix_chain.label: Pattern
config_change_fix_chain.pitfall: A config change is quickly fixed or reverted.
config_change_fix_chain.signal: Config-glob commit C, fix/revert D within 72h or <=10 commits touching same key/line range; weight same-author; exclude bots, version bumps.
config_change_fix_chain.question: What was wrong and what check would catch it?
config_change_fix_chain.example: Timeout 30 meant seconds but unit is ms; fixed next day.

config_default_flip.name: Configuration default value flipped
config_default_flip.label: AntiPattern
config_default_flip.pitfall: Changed code/shipped default silently changes every deployment relying on it.
config_default_flip.signal: Changed numeric/bool default literal (getenv default, argparse, Field, viper) or values/defaults YAML, key with >=2 read-sites or in shipped defaults; ratio >=2x or bool flip; skip moves; boost no docs/changelog change.
config_default_flip.packet: Key, old/new, consumers, doc changes, fixes.
config_default_flip.question: Did behaviour change for default users?

orphaned_ownership_legacy_core.name: Core module whose knowledgeable authors have all left
orphaned_ownership_legacy_core.label: AntiPattern
orphaned_ownership_legacy_core.pitfall: Newcomers change files whose owners are gone, with higher defect rates.
orphaned_ownership_legacy_core.signal: Owners (>=70% share, identities merged) inactive >=12 months; file >=20 commits or top-decile in-degree; non-owner fix-lineage commit within 12 months; >=3 non-trivial departed-owner messages.
orphaned_ownership_legacy_core.packet: Ownership over time, outsider changes and fixes, owner messages.
orphaned_ownership_legacy_core.question: What invariants did departed authors encode?
orphaned_ownership_legacy_core.noise: Merge aliases, skip bots, small files, repos <1 year or <2 authors.
orphaned_ownership_legacy_core.example: Scheduler file 90% by two former maintainers gets three one-off fixes.

coverage_threshold_lowered.name: Coverage gate lowered or exclusions grown
coverage_threshold_lowered.label: AntiPattern
coverage_threshold_lowered.pitfall: fail_under/coverageThreshold lowered, or omit/pragma: no cover/istanbul ignore additions growing to keep the gate green.
coverage_threshold_lowered.why: Coverage is a changelist-level signal not a target (Ivankovic 2019; Inozemtseva & Holmes); gaming makes the gate meaningless.
coverage_threshold_lowered.signal: Track values of fail_under, --cov-fail-under, [tool.coverage] omit/exclude_lines, coverageThreshold, codecov target and `# pragma: no cover` / `istanbul ignore` counts across history. Candidate events: any threshold decrease of >=2 points, a new omit entry covering a file with fix history or fan_in above the median, or pragma count up >=5 over 90 days. Suppress pragmas on TYPE_CHECKING, __repr__, abstract, NotImplementedError and __main__, and omit entries that match generated paths.
coverage_threshold_lowered.packet: Threshold timeline; newly excluded files/lines with risk and fix lineage; test links; what exclusions guard.
coverage_threshold_lowered.question: Legitimate exclusions or hiding hard-to-test risky code? What seam would let a test cover excluded risky code?
coverage_threshold_lowered.noise: Pragma on TYPE_CHECKING, NotImplementedError, __repr__, abstract, __main__; drops after large generated code with matching omit; <1 point drops recovered.
coverage_threshold_lowered.example: fail_under 85 to 70 in 'make CI green' and db/migrations.py added to omit; it has 5 fixes.

emergency_commit_followup_chain.name: Emergency change followed by fix-ups
emergency_commit_followup_chain.label: Pattern
emergency_commit_followup_chain.pitfall: Hotfixes pushed unreviewed are followed by corrections.
emergency_commit_followup_chain.signal: Word-boundary hotfix|emergency|sev[0-4]|p0|outage|rollback|stopgap message (no 'urgent' in feat/docs) with >=1 fix/revert on same file within 72h; rank chain length, revert end, temporary markers.
emergency_commit_followup_chain.question: What was the real fix?
emergency_commit_followup_chain.example: hotfix: bump timeout, then revert and use retry.

error_branch_untested.name: Error and exception paths never exercised
error_branch_untested.label: AntiPattern
error_branch_untested.pitfall: Success path covered but except/raise/guard/error-return branches (especially those added by fixes) are never executed.
error_branch_untested.why: Yuan et al. (OSDI 2014): 92% of catastrophic failures stem from incorrect handling of non-fatal errors, 58% catchable by simple tests of handlers. Oracle already has error-handling findings and fix-lineage guard types.
error_branch_untested.signal: Take guard lines added by fix commits (raise, except, none_check, early return, taken from existing fix-lineage guard types). With coverage: the guard line has zero hits at HEAD. Without coverage: none of the symbol's linked tests contains raises/assertRaises/toThrow/side_effect/mockRejectedValue or an empty/None literal argument. Require the function to have at least one linked test. Zero-test symbols belong to the no-test candidates. Add fan_in>=2 or >=2 fix edits to the handler. Exclude ImportError probes, TYPE_CHECKING, NotImplementedError, pragma no cover and log-and-reraise. Fold the I/O retry/timeout cases into this candidate as a priority boost, not a separate type.
error_branch_untested.packet: Function with error branches marked; fix commit introducing each guard; line coverage; callers and what they expect on failure; linked tests and inputs; mutation survivors.
error_branch_untested.question: Which failure can actually occur (I/O, parse, missing key, timeout) and what must the handler do (propagate, retry, default)? Give the injected failure and exact assertion; contractual vs defensive-only (then skip or delete).
error_branch_untested.noise: except ImportError probes, KeyboardInterrupt, TYPE_CHECKING, NotImplementedError, assert_never, pragma: no cover, log-and-reraise handlers, fan_in 0 with no fix history.
error_branch_untested.example: charge() catches TimeoutError and retries; fix added a retry cap raising PaymentFailed; no test injects a timeout.
sources: Yuan et al., Simple Testing Can Prevent Most Critical Failures, OSDI 2014
Gunawi et al., What Bugs Live in the Cloud, SoCC 2014

exception_hierarchy_reparenting.name: Exception class re-parented
exception_hierarchy_reparenting.label: AntiPattern
exception_hierarchy_reparenting.pitfall: Base-class changes alter which handlers catch the error.
exception_hierarchy_reparenting.why: Handlers start catching or missing errors.
exception_hierarchy_reparenting.signal: INHERITS base-list change of *Error/*Exception class or new intermediate class; >=2 catch sites with differing handler bodies; rank by sites naming old/new base.
exception_hierarchy_reparenting.packet: Class diff, hierarchy, catch and raise sites.
exception_hierarchy_reparenting.question: Which handlers catch a different set?
exception_hierarchy_reparenting.noise: Test helpers, identical handlers, new classes.
exception_hierarchy_reparenting.example: PaymentTimeout under NetworkError starts being retried.

expand_contract_incomplete.name: Expand phase without contract (dual-write leftover)
expand_contract_incomplete.label: Pattern
expand_contract_incomplete.pitfall: Shadow columns stay forever beside the old ones.
expand_contract_incomplete.signal: Columns/tables matching _new|_old|_legacy|_v2|_bak|_tmp added by migration, no later DROP, age >180d, both present at HEAD; rank HEAD readers/writers; co-assignment as boost.
expand_contract_incomplete.question: Which is authoritative?
expand_contract_incomplete.example: users.email_new and users.email both written for two years.

per_request_client_construction.name: Expensive client constructed per call
per_request_client_construction.label: AntiPattern
per_request_client_construction.pitfall: HTTP/DB/boto clients built per request cause socket churn and exhaustion.
per_request_client_construction.signal: Fix moving client constructor to module/class scope or message reuse client|TIME_WAIT; or constructor in function with in-degree>=3/route decorator; exclude get_client/create_*/init.
per_request_client_construction.question: Intentional per-tenant or defect?
per_request_client_construction.example: new HttpClient per request exhausted sockets.

flaky_test_markers.name: Flaky test markers and quarantines
flaky_test_markers.label: AntiPattern
flaky_test_markers.pitfall: Retries, reruns, sleeps and 'fix flaky' commits mark nondeterministic tests whose results get ignored, hiding real regressions.
flaky_test_markers.why: Async wait, concurrency and order are top flaky causes (Luo 2014); ~16% of Google tests show flakiness; flakes may mask real races.
flaky_test_markers.signal: Match commit messages on flak|intermittent|sporadic|rerun|retry|timing|race in commits that touch test files, and match added diff lines containing @flaky, reruns=, retryTimes, pytest.mark.skip with a flaky reason, raised timeouts or new sleep() calls in tests. Group per test file or test function and flag >=2 marker commits or a test touched >=3 times in such commits. Join the mapped subject's race-zone fixes or safety findings. Exclude infra-only commits and sleeps in rate-limit tests.
flaky_test_markers.packet: Marker commits and diffs; test body; target and race findings; root-cause category guess.
flaky_test_markers.question: Root-cause category and deterministic replacement (fake clock, event wait, fixture isolation)? Does the flake mask a real race in production?
flaky_test_markers.noise: Intentional rate-limit/timeout test sleeps; retries in production code; CI-infra-only commits.
flaky_test_markers.example: test_worker_shutdown got @flaky(reruns=3); Worker.stop has a race finding.

graceful_shutdown_signal_drift.name: Graceful shutdown, signal handling and PID 1 drift
graceful_shutdown_signal_drift.label: Pattern
graceful_shutdown_signal_drift.pitfall: Shell-form CMD, missing exec/tini, preStop, grace period and SIGTERM handlers must fit in-flight work.
graceful_shutdown_signal_drift.why: Rolling deploys drop requests; SIGKILL after grace.
graceful_shutdown_signal_drift.signal: Commits changing CMD/ENTRYPOINT form, wrapper (tini, dumb-init, exec removed from final line), terminationGracePeriodSeconds|preStop|stop_grace_period|STOPSIGNAL, or adding/removing SIGTERM/shutdown handlers; boost shutdown/SIGTERM/zombie messages within +/-10 commits; require long-running server signal.
graceful_shutdown_signal_drift.packet: Dockerfile/manifest timeline, handler bodies, shutdown commits.
graceful_shutdown_signal_drift.question: Does the final process receive SIGTERM and fit the grace period?
graceful_shutdown_signal_drift.noise: Skip dev Dockerfiles, build stages, exec "$@" entrypoints, batch tools.
graceful_shutdown_signal_drift.example: CMD npm start swallows SIGTERM; pods SIGKILLed after 30s.

guard_input_class_unfed.name: Guard for an input class (fixed or defensive) that no test feeds
guard_input_class_unfed.label: AntiPattern
guard_input_class_unfed.pitfall: Code guards against empty, None, zero, negative or duplicate input, either because a bug fix added the guard or because the author anticipated it, yet no linked test feeds that input class (or the only test that did was deleted).
guard_input_class_unfed.why: Category-partition testing needs one test frame per input category; a fix guard is direct proof the partition is reachable in production and failing, and a defensive guard at HEAD is the proactive version. Partition testing only helps when partitions are the failing ones (Hamlet and Taylor); mutants in conditionals are what tests miss most (Just et al.). Existing fix-without-regression-test asks only whether any test changed, not whether the right class was fed.
guard_input_class_unfed.signal: Restrict to variant A. Take a fix commit in a non-bulk, non-reverted zone whose added lines inside a mapped function body match a small guard regex set (empty, None, zero, negative). Require that the fix commit did not touch any linked test AND that no linked-test call literal or parametrize value labels to the same class. Where imported coverage exists, require the guard line to have zero hits. Rank by symbol fix count times risk score. Fold in the numeric zero/negative and malformed-input classes as extra labels instead of separate kinds. Drop variant B, or emit it only when measured coverage shows the guard line never executed.
guard_input_class_unfed.packet: Fix hunk and message (or git-blame commit introducing the guard); function body with guard lines marked; class label; per-parameter table of test literals by class with link source and weight; trimmed linked-test bodies; callers that can pass the class with call-site literals; signature; later commits to the function; measured line hits if available.
guard_input_class_unfed.question: Can a caller really deliver class C (not excluded by type hint or validated callers), and what single parametrized case with what expected output or exception would have failed before commit X? Or is the guard dead weight to remove or leave untested?
guard_input_class_unfed.noise: Drop when type hint excludes the class (non-Optional, NonEmpty, Literal) and callers pass validated values; drop generated/vendored/migrations/minified code; drop guards that only log; drop self/cls guards and `if x is None: x = default` normalisation covered by omitting the argument; drop when coverage-measured test hits the guard AND a literal of the class is present (check actual value since truthiness guards fire for 0 and ''); skip private helpers with <2 callers and no public API flag; ignore bulk commits.
guard_input_class_unfed.example: parse_ref() got `if not ref: return None` in commit a1b2 after a crash on empty string; tests/test_refs.py parametrizes 6 cases, all non-empty. Recommend test_parse_ref_empty asserting None and no exception.
sources: Ostrand and Balcer, The Category-Partition Method for Specifying and Generating Functional Tests, CACM 31(6), 1988
Hamlet and Taylor, Partition Testing Does Not Inspire Confidence, IEEE TSE 1990
Ammann and Offutt, Introduction to Software Testing, Ch.4 Input Space Partitioning
Just et al., Are Mutants a Valid Substitute for Real Faults in Software Testing?, FSE 2014
Ivankovic et al., Code Coverage at Google, ESEC/FSE 2019

http_cache_header_policy_change.name: HTTP cache directive / Vary policy change
http_cache_header_policy_change.label: AntiPattern
http_cache_header_policy_change.signal: public/s-maxage/cache_page added or private/no-store/Vary removed on non-static route whose handler reads session/cookie/user/Authorization; or proxy_cache_key change; drop plain max-age/ETag.
http_cache_header_policy_change.packet: Header diff, handler body, later fixes.
http_cache_header_policy_change.question: Can a shared cache store a per-user response?

fix_prone_high_fan_in_hub.name: High fan-in symbol with fix history
fix_prone_high_fan_in_hub.label: AntiPattern
fix_prone_high_fan_in_hub.pitfall: Hub symbols with repeated fixes spread blast radius (Hyrum's Law).
fix_prone_high_fan_in_hub.signal: Fan-in >=p95 (>=15 callers across >=4 dirs), >=3 fixes, at least one fix followed within 30 days by edits in >=2 caller files. Cap caller lists by directory.
fix_prone_high_fan_in_hub.packet: Body, callers by dir, fixes, follow-up caller changes.
fix_prone_high_fan_in_hub.question: What implicit behaviour do callers depend on?
fix_prone_high_fan_in_hub.example: Network measures found 60% of critical Windows binaries.
sources: Winters et al., SWE at Google

inprocess_scheduler_multi_instance.name: In-process scheduler under multi-process deployment
inprocess_scheduler_multi_instance.label: AntiPattern
inprocess_scheduler_multi_instance.pitfall: Schedulers in web process run once per worker.
inprocess_scheduler_multi_instance.signal: Scheduler intro regex then within 30 commits a guard (advisory_lock, WERKZEUG_RUN_MAIN, redlock, SET NX, flock, is_leader) or move to CronJob/Procfile; boost side-effecting job bodies.
inprocess_scheduler_multi_instance.packet: Intro, guard commit, process config, job body.
inprocess_scheduler_multi_instance.question: What ensures single execution?
inprocess_scheduler_multi_instance.noise: Idempotent jobs, no multi-worker config, tests.
inprocess_scheduler_multi_instance.example: Digest sent 4x with 4 workers; Redis lock added.

index_add_drop_readd_cycle.name: Index added, dropped and re-added
index_add_drop_readd_cycle.label: RejectedAttempt
index_add_drop_readd_cycle.pitfall: Index flips record unwritten query-plan lessons.
index_add_drop_readd_cycle.why: Dropping needed index causes scans; re-add locks writes.
index_add_drop_readd_cycle.signal: Normalise (table, ordered columns); create/drop/create with >=3 events in >=2 commits, or drop followed by create with different predicate/uniqueness/order even with 2 events; raw SQL, Alembic, Rails first.
index_add_drop_readd_cycle.packet: Ordered events, DDL diff, nearby queries.
index_add_drop_readd_cycle.question: Why dropped and why back in different form?
index_add_drop_readd_cycle.example: Index re-added as partial after slow-report incident.

interface_change_broke_seam.name: Interface change followed by a downstream fix in another package
interface_change_broke_seam.label: AntiPattern
interface_change_broke_seam.pitfall: A callee's signature, return shape or raised exceptions changed and soon after a fix had to change cross-package callers: the seam broke and nothing caught it at the change.
interface_change_broke_seam.why: Change propagation across boundaries is the classic integration failure; logical coupling predicts defects (D'Ambros et al.; Hassan and Holt). Each pair is retrospective proof the seam was untested at that moment and the break shape says what a seam test should assert.
interface_change_broke_seam.signal: C1 = commit where a symbol's parameter list, return annotation, or raise/return-site count changed (hash of the signature plus raise set). C2 = classified fix commit within 30 days or 20 main-line commits that touches a file in a different top-level package, with the symbol name appearing as a token in the C2 diff hunk or message. Use HEAD callers only as a hint, and do not require C1 to have edited any caller. Require C2 to modify a caller and not the callee. Rank by shorter gap and by whether C1 edited no cross-package file.
interface_change_broke_seam.packet: C1 signature diff; cross-package callers at C1 and which were edited; C2 message and caller diff; tests changed in C1 and C2; current tests on the edge.
interface_change_broke_seam.question: Was C2 a consequence of C1? Would a cross-package test through the real caller have failed at C1, with what assertion, or would a type checker have caught it?
interface_change_broke_seam.noise: Renames, docstring/format changes, bulk commits, unrelated C2; same-package callers; C2 touching only the callee again.
interface_change_broke_seam.example: Commit a1f changed fetch_commits() to return a generator; 9 days later fix b27 patched the dashboard builder calling len() on it. Add a seam test on the builder with a real fetch result.
sources: Hassan and Holt, Predicting change propagation in software systems, ICSM 2004

mass_automated_refactor_regression.name: Large automated refactor followed by fixes
mass_automated_refactor_regression.label: Pattern
mass_automated_refactor_regression.why: Fixes reveal what mechanical transforms miss.
mass_automated_refactor_regression.signal: Bulk/>=50-file commit with refactor message (non-AST-equal), then fix-classified commits within 30 days touching same symbols (>=3 or 10%).
mass_automated_refactor_regression.question: What did the transform miss?
mass_automated_refactor_regression.noise: Formatting, generated, license headers, initial import.
mass_automated_refactor_regression.example: Rename across 200 files shadows an override.

log_verbosity_flip.name: Log level or volume changed
log_verbosity_flip.label: Pattern
log_verbosity_flip.pitfall: Demoted levels hide alertable errors; DEBUG in prod costs money.
log_verbosity_flip.why: Monitors may depend on the line or level.
log_verbosity_flip.signal: (a) same message literal level demoted (error->warn/info); (b) config log-level key changed >=3 times or to debug in prod path; optional boost if alert rule references it.
log_verbosity_flip.packet: Level diffs, literal, fix commit, alert refs.
log_verbosity_flip.question: Did a monitor depend on this line?
log_verbosity_flip.noise: Skip tests/dev, CLIs, bulk logging refactors.
log_verbosity_flip.example: error('payment gateway timeout') demoted; paging alert never fires.

migration_followed_by_hotfix_migration.name: Migration followed by corrective migration
migration_followed_by_hotfix_migration.label: RejectedAttempt
migration_followed_by_hotfix_migration.pitfall: Quick alters of the same column signal a wrong first design.
migration_followed_by_hotfix_migration.signal: Group migrations on same (table,column) within 14 days via add/alter/AlterField/RenameField regexes; >=2 alterations; boost fix-style messages.
migration_followed_by_hotfix_migration.question: What was wrong with the first choice?
migration_followed_by_hotfix_migration.example: VARCHAR(50) to 255 to TEXT in days.

n_plus_one_fix_regression.name: N+1 fix lineage and likely regression
n_plus_one_fix_regression.label: Pattern
n_plus_one_fix_regression.pitfall: Eager-loading fixes are later undone by query changes.
n_plus_one_fix_regression.signal: Commit adds eager-load token (select_related, prefetch_related, joinedload, includes, DataLoader) absent pre-fix; later commit on same symbol/model removes it or a later fix recurs on same model/file.
n_plus_one_fix_regression.packet: Fix diff, later diffs, model relations.
n_plus_one_fix_regression.question: What access pattern must stay eager?
n_plus_one_fix_regression.noise: Skip migrations, admin scripts, small constant loops.
n_plus_one_fix_regression.example: Rails apps repeat the same N+1 patterns.

external_call_inside_transaction.name: Network/queue call inside transaction and commit-vs-publish fixes
external_call_inside_transaction.label: AntiPattern
external_call_inside_transaction.pitfall: Publishing inside a transaction causes ghost events and lock holds.
external_call_inside_transaction.signal: Primary: diff adds on_commit/afterCommit/outbox adjacent to removed publish/enqueue in same function (or reverse); message on_commit|ghost|not yet committed; HEAD scan only for direct siblings at depth 0-1.
external_call_inside_transaction.packet: Function, moving commits, sibling publish sites.
external_call_inside_transaction.question: Is ordering deliberate; which siblings violate?
external_call_inside_transaction.example: delay() inside atomic; moved to on_commit.

container_user_readonly_fs_change.name: Non-root/read-only rootfs tightening followed by write-path fixes
container_user_readonly_fs_change.label: Pattern
container_user_readonly_fs_change.pitfall: Hardening breaks writes and low ports; fixes are undocumented.
container_user_readonly_fs_change.signal: Tightening regex (USER final stage, runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, drop ALL) followed within 20 commits by emptyDir|tmpfs|chown|TMPDIR|HOME|XDG_CACHE_HOME, port >=1024, or hardening revert.
container_user_readonly_fs_change.question: Which paths must stay writable?

nondeterministic_iteration_fix_siblings.name: Ordering-nondeterminism fix with unfixed siblings
nondeterministic_iteration_fix_siblings.label: Pattern
nondeterministic_iteration_fix_siblings.why: Same assumption repeats in serializers and keys.
nondeterministic_iteration_fix_siblings.signal: Fix adds sorted()/sort_keys=True/sort before join/hash; siblings in same function as hashlib|hmac|digest|etag|cache_key|signature token lacking it; cap ~5.
nondeterministic_iteration_fix_siblings.packet: Fix diff, siblings with sink, tests.
nondeterministic_iteration_fix_siblings.question: Does sibling feed an order-sensitive consumer?
nondeterministic_iteration_fix_siblings.example: Cache key json.dumps gains sort_keys; two others omit it.

parallel_implementation_drift.name: Parallel v1/v2 or legacy/new implementations changed asymmetrically
parallel_implementation_drift.label: Pattern
parallel_implementation_drift.pitfall: Both versions stay live and fixes land on one side only.
parallel_implementation_drift.why: Names the canonical side and missing fixes.
parallel_implementation_drift.signal: Pair symbols/dirs by name transform (_v2, legacy_, v1/v2), both with callers; one side gets >=2 fix commits since the other's last change. Prefer same-module; exclude frozen API versions, proto/generated; dedupe with clone divergence.
parallel_implementation_drift.packet: Both bodies, diaries, one-sided fixes, caller counts.
parallel_implementation_drift.question: Which side is canonical and which fixes are missing?
parallel_implementation_drift.example: send_email_v2 gets a retry fix while send_email serves 40 call sites.

payload_and_message_size_limit_drift.name: Payload and message size limits mismatched across layers
payload_and_message_size_limit_drift.label: Pattern
payload_and_message_size_limit_drift.pitfall: Limits at different layers must nest; one-layer changes cause 413, truncation or stalls.
payload_and_message_size_limit_drift.why: Cloudflare Nov 2025 outage from file exceeding preallocated limit.
payload_and_message_size_limit_drift.signal: Fix commit (413|payload too large|truncat) touching a limit key, or limit key changed >=2x; HEAD cross-layer disagreement only when >=2 keys of one family present (Kafka broker/consumer, nginx/app).
payload_and_message_size_limit_drift.packet: All limit values, timeline, generator code.
payload_and_message_size_limit_drift.question: What size ordering must hold?
payload_and_message_size_limit_drift.example: Raising message.max.bytes without fetch.max.bytes stalls consumers.

enum_value_persisted_change.name: Persisted enum value renumbered or renamed
enum_value_persisted_change.label: Pattern
enum_value_persisted_change.pitfall: Reordered/inserted enum members change stored meaning.
enum_value_persisted_change.signal: Member inserted mid-body in implicit/ordinal enum, explicit value changed/reused, or member removed; boost when enum used in model fields/migrations/serializers; exclude pure appends.
enum_value_persisted_change.question: Are stored values interpreted the same?
enum_value_persisted_change.example: PENDING inserted at top of IntEnum.

platform_config_branch_unexercised.name: Platform, environment or flag branch no test runs
platform_config_branch_unexercised.label: AntiPattern
platform_config_branch_unexercised.pitfall: Branches on sys.platform/os.name/process.platform/Python-Node version, env vars, feature flags or CLI options execute on one CI config only, so fixes in the other arm have no tests.
platform_config_branch_unexercised.why: Configuration-dependent faults escape single-config coverage (Xu 2015; Rabkin & Katz 2011); 11% of Python projects have OS-dependent test failures (MSR 2026); Oracle's own Windows hang (e220ae2).
platform_config_branch_unexercised.signal: Restrict to platform/OS conditionals. Fire when the function has a conditional on platform or os.name, has >=1 fix commit mentioning an OS name, and no test references the platform string (monkeypatch or skipif) or the CI matrix lacks that OS. Drop env-var, flag and version arms for v1. Exclude setup/build scripts and __main__ blocks.
platform_config_branch_unexercised.packet: Conditional with both arms; coverage per side; fix commits; CI matrix excerpt; skipif/monkeypatch tests; env docs; setenv values.
platform_config_branch_unexercised.question: Which environment executes the untested arm? Can monkeypatching (sys.platform, os.sep, setenv) test it, or is a matrix OS needed? Is it a security-relevant switch? Give the assertion distinguishing the arms, or call it a dead fallback.
platform_config_branch_unexercised.noise: TYPE_CHECKING, __main__, versions below supported minimum, setup/build scripts, logging-level and CI/PYTHONUNBUFFERED probes, arms already run per coverage contexts, unsupported platforms, secrets read once without branching.
platform_config_branch_unexercised.example: if sys.platform=='win32': creationflags=... never runs on Linux CI; patch sys.platform and assert Popen kwargs.
sources: Xu et al., Too Many Knobs, FSE 2015
Silva, Farahat, d'Amorim, Cross-OS Portability in Python, MSR 2026

protective_control_removed.name: Protective control removed in a refactor
protective_control_removed.label: AntiPattern
protective_control_removed.pitfall: Rate limiters, timeouts, limits, probes removed inside unrelated refactors.
protective_control_removed.why: Guards matter only in rare failures (Knight Capital).
protective_control_removed.signal: Removed lines matching narrow vocabulary (circuit breaker, rate limit, max_size, timeout=, resources.limits, probes, PDB, killswitch) whose blame origin is a fix-lineage commit and no equivalent re-added in commit/file.
protective_control_removed.question: Was removal deliberate or collateral?
protective_control_removed.noise: Equivalents added, bulk, deleted files, tests.

proxy_buffering_streaming_upgrade_change.name: Proxy buffering/upgrade settings vs streaming endpoints
proxy_buffering_streaming_upgrade_change.label: Pattern
proxy_buffering_streaming_upgrade_change.signal: Changed buffering/Upgrade/X-Accel-Buffering line AND streaming/websocket symbol or string at HEAD (text/event-stream, StreamingResponse, EventSource); gzip only when streaming present.
proxy_buffering_streaming_upgrade_change.packet: Config diff, streaming handlers, later fixes.
proxy_buffering_streaming_upgrade_change.question: Which endpoints need unbuffered paths?
proxy_buffering_streaming_upgrade_change.example: X-Accel-Buffering: no dropped in nginx refactor.

pure_function_roundtrip_property_candida.name: Pure encode/decode or normalise function pair with example-only tests
pure_function_roundtrip_property_candida.label: AntiPattern
pure_function_roundtrip_property_candida.pitfall: Pure functions with an algebraic law (parse/format, encode/decode, serialize/deserialize, idempotent normalise, sort permutation, merge associativity) are tested only with hand-picked examples and have fix history.
pure_function_roundtrip_property_candida.why: QuickCheck showed one stated property replaces hundreds of examples and finds inputs authors did not think of; Goldstein et al. (ICSE 2024) report property tests are valued for exactly these laws. Highest return for Hypothesis because the oracle is the law itself. Complements serialization-migration-roundtrip-untested (schema migrations over time).
pure_function_roundtrip_property_candida.signal: Require the pair to be in the same module or class, both halves pure (no I/O, time or random in the transitive call graph to depth 2), at least one fix on either half or >=3 callers, no hypothesis/fast-check given covering the pair, and a type hint on the input for strategy derivation. Include idempotent normalise/canonical/sanitize functions (idempotence law only). Rank by fix count.
pure_function_roundtrip_property_candida.packet: Both bodies, signatures and type hints (to derive strategies); existing tests of each; fix hunks showing the breaking input class; callers; whether hypothesis is a dev dependency.
pure_function_roundtrip_property_candida.question: What is the law (round trip, idempotence, order- or length-preserving), what strategy (type hints plus fix classes), which failing example to pin with @example, and is the function pure enough for a flake-free property?
pure_function_roundtrip_property_candida.noise: Skip lossy conversions where the law is false (use idempotence only); functions using network/time/random; generated serializers.
pure_function_roundtrip_property_candida.example: encode_ref()/decode_ref() in refs.py: 4 example tests, 3 fixes for ':' and '/' in names. Property decode(encode(s)) == s over text() with @example('a:b/c').
sources: MacIver, Hatfield-Dodds et al., Hypothesis, JOSS 2019
Goldstein et al., Property-Based Testing in Practice, ICSE 2024

time_bug_hotspot.name: Recurring time, timezone and calendar bugs
time_bug_hotspot.label: AntiPattern
time_bug_hotspot.pitfall: DST, leap, naive datetimes, wall clocks for durations recur.
time_bug_hotspot.signal: Fix-classified commits with time-keyword messages whose diff touches datetime/time APIs; >=2 per file/symbol or 1 plus wall-clock duration arithmetic; exclude format/log/fixtures.
time_bug_hotspot.question: Which time invariant is violated?
time_bug_hotspot.example: Negative duration after leap second panics RRDNS.

regression_after_refactor.name: Refactoring followed by a fix on the same code
regression_after_refactor.label: AntiPattern
regression_after_refactor.why: Marks code where restructuring is unsafe.
regression_after_refactor.signal: Fix within 60 days whose SZZ origin is a refactor commit (diary moved/extracted or sim>=0.85 pair, or refactor-style message) with >=10 behavioural lines; drop identifier-only renames.
regression_after_refactor.question: Which semantic detail was lost?
regression_after_refactor.noise: Exclude renames, >=95% similar moves, formatters, bulk.

post_release_hotfix_cluster.name: Release followed by hotfix burst
post_release_hotfix_cluster.label: Pattern
post_release_hotfix_cluster.pitfall: Post-release fixes reveal what the release got wrong.
post_release_hotfix_cluster.why: Shows change classes that escaped testing.
post_release_hotfix_cluster.signal: Tags (or version-bump commits) followed by patch tag or >=3 fix commits within 14 days touching symbols/files changed in preceding release; boost config/migration/Dockerfile.
post_release_hotfix_cluster.question: Which categories escaped testing?

read_after_write_replica_fix.name: Replica lag or read-your-writes fix
read_after_write_replica_fix.label: Pattern
read_after_write_replica_fix.pitfall: Reads routed to lagging replicas after writes.
read_after_write_replica_fix.why: Each fix marks a path that must read from primary.
read_after_write_replica_fix.signal: Message match (replica lag|read-your-writes|stale read) or primary-routing token diff (using('default'), use_primary, DATABASE_ROUTERS) within a fix-classified commit; no bare sticky/lsn.
read_after_write_replica_fix.question: Which paths need primary consistency?
read_after_write_replica_fix.example: Redirect page 404s from replica; route to primary 2s.

retention_and_backup_reduction.name: Retention, backup or lifecycle policy shortened
retention_and_backup_reduction.label: Pattern
retention_and_backup_reduction.pitfall: Retention cut for cost destroys recovery/forensics.
retention_and_backup_reduction.signal: Parse unit-normalised decreases >=2x or to 0/1 or removal on retention|backup_retention_period|expiration|message_retention|keepLast|revisionHistoryLimit keys, excluding cache/CI-artifact/dev paths.
retention_and_backup_reduction.question: What recovery capability depends on it?

cookie_attribute_change.name: Session/auth cookie attribute or name changed
cookie_attribute_change.label: Pattern
cookie_attribute_change.pitfall: Name/Domain/SameSite/Secure changes cause mass logout or loops.
cookie_attribute_change.signal: Settings-style keys (SESSION_COOKIE_*, CSRF_COOKIE_*, session middleware options) value changes in name/domain/samesite/secure; generic set_cookie only when name matches sess|auth|token|sid.
cookie_attribute_change.question: Effect on existing sessions?

api_signature_change_then_callsite_fix.name: Signature change followed by late call-site fix-ups
api_signature_change_then_callsite_fix.label: AntiPattern
api_signature_change_then_callsite_fix.pitfall: Callers invisible to static tools are fixed only later.
api_signature_change_then_callsite_fix.signal: Public symbol param/default change, then >=2 commits within 14 days touching caller files or files NOT in CALLS graph that textually reference the symbol; boost error-word messages; skip if original commit updated all callers.
api_signature_change_then_callsite_fix.question: Which callers are invisible?
api_signature_change_then_callsite_fix.example: Function gains required arg; plugin dir breaks 3 days later.

contract_one_side_tested.name: String contract with an untested producer or consumer
contract_one_side_tested.label: AntiPattern
contract_one_side_tested.pitfall: Two sides coupled by a string key (route, event, config key, SQL column, JSON field) where tests cover one side, so a rename breaks the other silently.
contract_one_side_tested.why: String-coupled interfaces fail at runtime; consumer-driven contract testing exists for this. Oracle already extracts string contracts.
contract_one_side_tested.signal: Require a literal >=6 chars with producer and consumer in different files (ideally different languages or packages), >=3 usages, and zero test files containing the literal or an indirect route-level test. Boost when the literal was renamed or a fix touched either side in history, or when a co-change pair links both sides. Exclude i18n/log strings and literals defined once as an imported constant.
contract_one_side_tested.packet: Literal; producer and consumer sites; tests containing it; coverage per site; literal history and related fixes.
contract_one_side_tested.question: If someone renames this key at one site, would any test fail? Propose a round-trip test or a shared constant, whichever is cheaper.
contract_one_side_tested.noise: Literals <4 chars or common words; log/user-facing text; already a single imported constant.
contract_one_side_tested.example: '/api/risk/files' served by a tested handler but fetched in untested HealthStrip.tsx; renaming the route passes all tests.

adr_superseded_code_remains.name: Superseded ADR whose implementation is still live
adr_superseded_code_remains.label: AntiPattern
adr_superseded_code_remains.pitfall: Old-decision code persists as a half-migrated layer.
adr_superseded_code_remains.signal: ADR status Superseded/Deprecated/Rejected; >=2 non-generic backticked tokens (>=1 package/path/class) resolve at HEAD and >=1 modified after status date; exclude tokens in successor decision.
adr_superseded_code_remains.packet: ADR sections, status commit, successor, post-supersession commits.
adr_superseded_code_remains.question: Is live code the legacy form?
adr_superseded_code_remains.example: ADR Celery superseded by Arq; celery_app.py edited 14 times after.

surprise_defect_fix_in_quiet_file.name: Surprise fix in a previously quiet file
surprise_defect_fix_in_quiet_file.label: AntiPattern
surprise_defect_fix_in_quiet_file.pitfall: A dormant file breaks because of a change elsewhere.
surprise_defect_fix_in_quiet_file.signal: Fix on F dormant >=12 months, with G changed in prior 30 days linked by resolved import/call/contract or prior co-change; fix references G's symbol/key or adds a test exercising G. Max 2 pairs per fix.
surprise_defect_fix_in_quiet_file.packet: F fix, G commit, edges, dormancy.
surprise_defect_fix_in_quiet_file.question: What hidden dependency broke F?
surprise_defect_fix_in_quiet_file.noise: Exclude typo/doc/dep fixes, bulk, <3 code lines.
surprise_defect_fix_in_quiet_file.example: Fix in a file untouched for years.

synchronized_schedules_and_ttl_herd.name: Synchronized schedules (thundering herd)
synchronized_schedules_and_ttl_herd.label: AntiPattern
synchronized_schedules_and_ttl_herd.pitfall: Many cron jobs at the same minute hit shared resources.
synchronized_schedules_and_ttl_herd.why: Periodic spikes; stagger convention is non-obvious.
synchronized_schedules_and_ttl_herd.signal: Parse cron (k8s CronJob, celery beat, crontab, @Scheduled): >=4 jobs in one slot AND a job touching DB/HTTP client; always emit commits adding jitter|stagger|splay|singleflight or thundering herd/stampede messages. Exclude CI schedules.
synchronized_schedules_and_ttl_herd.packet: Slot table, adding commits, job bodies.
synchronized_schedules_and_ttl_herd.question: What shared resource is hit at once?
synchronized_schedules_and_ttl_herd.example: Eight CronJobs at 0 0 * * * hit the DB.

mock_the_subject.name: Test mocks the code it should test
mock_the_subject.label: AntiPattern
mock_the_subject.pitfall: A test patches the target or the collaborator holding its logic so real code never runs, yet the static link counts as protection.
mock_the_subject.why: Over-mocking weakens tests (Spadini 2017/2019; Mostafa & Wang 2014); the weight-1.0 link is false evidence feeding tests_to_run.
mock_the_subject.signal: Linked test whose patch/monkeypatch.setattr/jest.mock/vi.mock/spyOn target string resolves to (a) the linked symbol itself, or (b) the module-qualified name of the symbol the test is linked to. Mark the symbol 'mock-dominated' when every link is of this kind. Exclude clock/random/network/subprocess/env/filesystem targets and conftest autouse mocks. If coverage is imported, confirm by zero covered lines in the symbol from that test. Drop the callee-share heuristic.
mock_the_subject.packet: Test body with patch lines and resolved targets; target body; callee patched share; static vs coverage disagreement; other unmocked tests; fixes.
mock_the_subject.question: Does any test run the real logic? Which boundary is legitimate to fake? Write the test with real logic and faked boundary.
mock_the_subject.noise: Patches of clock, random, network, subprocess, env, filesystem, third-party SDKs; orchestration code where call order is the contract; autospec contract tests; conftest I/O-only mocks.
mock_the_subject.example: test_assess patches risk.score and asserts assess returns the patched value.
sources: Spadini et al., To Mock or Not To Mock?, MSR 2017

declared_domain_gap.name: Type-declared or defaulted input domain larger than the tested domain
declared_domain_gap.label: AntiPattern
declared_domain_gap.pitfall: The signature admits classes (Optional, Union, str | Path, Literal/Enum members, bool flags, defaulted options like strict=False, recursive=False, limit=None) and the body branches on them, but linked tests never pass the variants: no None, never Path, 2 of 5 enum members, flag always at default.
declared_domain_gap.why: Types and defaults give a cheap, high-precision statement of the partitions the author intends, applying Ostrand and Balcer categories automatically. Unseen enum members and union arms cause switch fallthrough defects, and an unexercised option arm is invisible to name and import links so the risk score treats the function as tested. Parameter-value classes interact (Kuhn).
declared_domain_gap.signal: Fire on (1) an enum member or Literal arm added in a recent commit whose name appears in no test file, or (2) a defaulted or Optional parameter that is added or changed in a commit after the last touch of its linked tests, appears in a body condition, is passed non-default by at least one non-test caller, and appears as a keyword in no linked test call. Skip pass-through parameters and logging flags. Rank by fan-in and fix count.
declared_domain_gap.packet: Signature and its history from the symbol diary (param added in commit X); body with arm-dependent branches; enum definition and member list; per-arm test usage table; non-test callers using each arm; last test touch date.
declared_domain_gap.question: Which untested arms have distinct behaviour worth pinning (not a shared default), and what single parametrized test over all enum members or a default-vs-non-default pair on the same input would catch a forgotten arm next time?
declared_domain_gap.noise: Skip enums used only as labels/log fields; arms sharing one default path; Optional params normalised on the first line; params that only pass through to another function; logging/verbosity flags; DI-only params for fakes.
declared_domain_gap.example: render(kind: Kind) has 6 members; tests use Kind.A and Kind.B; Kind.F added in 91ab takes the else branch. collect(paths, recursive=False) gained recursive in d00f and the CLI passes True, no test does. Add parametrize over list(Kind) and a nested-dir case.
sources: Ammann and Offutt, Input Space Partitioning (interface-based partitioning)
Kuhn, Wallace and Gallo, IEEE TSE 2004
Claessen and Hughes, QuickCheck, ICFP 2000 (generators from types)

unique_constraint_semantics_change.name: Unique or partial index predicate changed
unique_constraint_semantics_change.label: AntiPattern
unique_constraint_semantics_change.pitfall: Changed uniqueness breaks ON CONFLICT targets and dedup.
unique_constraint_semantics_change.signal: Normalised unique definition of same name/column set differs in predicate, UNIQUE flag or order; attach code evidence only when table/model name appears in file with conflict/unique-violation pattern.
unique_constraint_semantics_change.question: Do upsert targets still match?
unique_constraint_semantics_change.example: email unique becomes partial; ON CONFLICT (email) fails.

composition_root_untested.name: Wiring and registration tables with repeated 'forgot to register' fixes
composition_root_untested.label: AntiPattern
composition_root_untested.pitfall: Composition code (route tables, tool registries, CLI subcommand lists, DI containers, entry_points) glues packages together; units are tested but forgetting or mis-wiring registration is caught only by users.
composition_root_untested.why: Wiring defects are interface defects at the composition root, and cheap enumeration tests (every registered tool callable, every route has a handler) are among the highest-value medium tests.
composition_root_untested.signal: Per file, count commits in the fix lineage or with a <=5-line diff whose added lines match registration idioms and where the registered symbol was created in an earlier commit. Flag files with >=2 such follow-ups, and no test importing that registry file and iterating its entries. Skip the 'unregistered at HEAD' check at first.
composition_root_untested.packet: Registry file; follow-up commit pairs; current listing; unregistered symbols at HEAD; tests mapped to the registry.
composition_root_untested.question: Is there a set-completeness invariant? Specify a test enumerating by reflection or glob, comparing to the registry, plus one end-to-end call per entry.
composition_root_untested.noise: Generated and single-entry registries; registries already iterated by a test; bulk initial scaffolding.
composition_root_untested.example: MCP tool 'assess_change' was registered one commit after its implementation following a user report; a third tool is unregistered at HEAD. Add a test comparing server tools to the handler module.
sources: Winters et al., ch.11-14 (medium tests, smoke tests)
Seemann, Composition Root, Dependency Injection in .NET, 2011
Ford, Parsons and Kua, Building Evolutionary Architectures, 2017

config_key_rename_orphan.name: Config key renamed or removed but still read
config_key_rename_orphan.label: AntiPattern
config_key_rename_orphan.pitfall: A key is renamed in config while code/overlays still use the old name, silently defaulting.
config_key_rename_orphan.signal: Removed/renamed structured keys (dotted >=2 segments or >8 chars) with literal reader still at HEAD in another file; skip env vars (use env contract kind); no Levenshtein pairing or loader variant.
config_key_rename_orphan.packet: Key diff, lingering references, code default.
config_key_rename_orphan.question: Is the reader silently on a default?
config_key_rename_orphan.example: Helm resources.limits.mem renamed; overlay keeps old key.

embedded_expiry_literal.name: Embedded expiry: certs, pins and dated literals
embedded_expiry_literal.label: AntiPattern
embedded_expiry_literal.pitfall: Committed certs/pins fire on a date, not a code change.
embedded_expiry_literal.signal: PEM notAfter within 365 days of latest commit or expired; pin/fingerprint strings with replacement history; cert files replaced >=2 times; date literals only on valid_until|not_after|expires keys; suppress with cert-manager/ACME config.
embedded_expiry_literal.question: What renews it and what breaks?
embedded_expiry_literal.example: Pinned CA fingerprint replaced only after expiry failures.

raise_contract_change_stale_callers.name: Failure contract changed while callers handle the old one
raise_contract_change_stale_callers.label: AntiPattern
raise_contract_change_stale_callers.pitfall: Raise vs return-None switches invalidate caller handlers.
raise_contract_change_stale_callers.signal: Python typed CALLS: changed raised class or None<->raise swap; callers within 15 lines with except OldClass or 'is None' check unmodified since; cap 5 callers by weight.
raise_contract_change_stale_callers.packet: Function diff, callers with handling, tests.
raise_contract_change_stale_callers.question: Do callers handle the new failure mode?
raise_contract_change_stale_callers.example: get_user() returns None; except UserNotFound never fires.

route_guard_partial_rollout.name: Guard rolled out to some sibling handlers only
route_guard_partial_rollout.label: AntiPattern
route_guard_partial_rollout.signal: Python decorators v1: commit adds same guard to >=2 handlers in a file/router; handler predating rollout lacks it; also guard removed from exactly one handler; exclude health|login|webhook|metrics|docs names.
route_guard_partial_rollout.question: Intentionally public or omission?
route_guard_partial_rollout.example: 9 of 10 admin handlers get @require_role; export_all missed.

k8s_immutable_or_deprecated_change.name: Kubernetes selector, label or immutable field change
k8s_immutable_or_deprecated_change.label: Pattern
k8s_immutable_or_deprecated_change.pitfall: Selector/label edits break other objects or force recreation.
k8s_immutable_or_deprecated_change.why: Services serve no endpoints; Pi-Day-style label contracts.
k8s_immutable_or_deprecated_change.signal: Non-templated YAML: changed spec.selector.matchLabels/volumeClaimTemplates or pod label removed; grep HEAD for old key=value in Service/NetworkPolicy/affinity/nodeSelector not changed in commit; apiVersion bumps as low tier.
k8s_immutable_or_deprecated_change.question: What else depends on this label?
k8s_immutable_or_deprecated_change.example: Service still selects old label after Deployment relabel.

mock_target_signature_drift.name: Mocked function changed signature, mock not updated
mock_target_signature_drift.label: AntiPattern
mock_target_signature_drift.pitfall: Unconstrained mocks keep passing when contracts change.
mock_target_signature_drift.signal: Python mock.patch full-string targets resolved to symbol S; diary shows param-list change; patching test file untouched within 14 days; boost no autospec and later caller fix.
mock_target_signature_drift.packet: Signature diff, mock sites, later caller fixes.
mock_target_signature_drift.question: Which tests do not bind S's contract?
mock_target_signature_drift.example: charge() gains currency; tests patching it pass.

alert_or_slo_loosened.name: Monitoring or alert rule loosened or deleted
alert_or_slo_loosened.label: AntiPattern
alert_or_slo_loosened.pitfall: Noisy alerts are relaxed or removed.
alert_or_slo_loosened.signal: alert/rule/monitor/slo files: threshold, for:, evaluation_periods, severity changed in loosening direction (comparator-aware) or alert removed/silenced; join incident commits on component within 90 days.
alert_or_slo_loosened.question: What would the old alert have caught?

orm_model_migration_drift.name: ORM model changed without migration
orm_model_migration_drift.label: Pattern
orm_model_migration_drift.pitfall: Model fields change without migrations or vice versa.
orm_model_migration_drift.signal: Field add/remove/retype in model class with sibling migrations dir and no migration on branch before merge; rank later 'missing migration' commit; Django and Alembic first.
orm_model_migration_drift.question: What sync convention was escaped?
orm_model_migration_drift.example: Column('archived') migration lands three commits later.

sibling_config_drift.name: Per-environment config twins that drifted apart
sibling_config_drift.label: AntiPattern
sibling_config_drift.pitfall: values-dev/prod, overlays and tfvars are copy-paste twins; a key is changed in one and forgotten in others.
sibling_config_drift.signal: Group files by env-token stem with line similarity >=0.7 at HEAD (>=3 files or 2 highly similar). Emit (a) key changed in one member while siblings keep old value 90+ days, (c) prod-only edit with no sibling change in prior 30 days; boost fix/revert within 7 days. Exclude host/url/replicas/account/region/secret keys.
sibling_config_drift.packet: Key-by-env matrix, key diff, per-sibling history, follow-ups.
sibling_config_drift.question: Deliberate tuning or unpropagated change?
sibling_config_drift.example: Timeout raised to 120s in values-prod.yaml while staging keeps 30s.

shotgun_surgery_commit_pattern.name: Recurring multi-file change with a forgotten file
shotgun_surgery_commit_pattern.label: Pattern
shotgun_surgery_commit_pattern.pitfall: One concept change needs edits in many files; omissions cause defects.
shotgun_surgery_commit_pattern.signal: File set of >=4 recurring in >=3 commits; another commit touches the set but misses a file, followed by a fix touching the missing file within 30 days.
shotgun_surgery_commit_pattern.packet: Recurring file sets, example hunks, forgotten-file follow-up.
shotgun_surgery_commit_pattern.question: What is the checklist for this change type?
shotgun_surgery_commit_pattern.noise: Skip releases, translations, lockfiles, generated, bulk renames.
shotgun_surgery_commit_pattern.example: Adding a payment method; one commit forgot the serializer.

retry_on_non_idempotent_write.name: Retry or redelivery around a non-idempotent side effect
retry_on_non_idempotent_write.label: AntiPattern
retry_on_non_idempotent_write.pitfall: Retries duplicate payments/emails/inserts without idempotency keys.
retry_on_non_idempotent_write.why: Duplicate side effects; the contract is easy to re-break.
retry_on_non_idempotent_write.signal: Retry/at-least-once scope (autoretry_for incl. Exception/timeouts) whose body or callees (depth<=3) hit curated sinks (requests.post, INSERT w/o ON CONFLICT, stripe/boto send/publish, sendmail) with no idempotency token; boost later duplicate/twice messages.
retry_on_non_idempotent_write.packet: Retry commit, body, sink, idempotency code.
retry_on_non_idempotent_write.question: Can replay duplicate the effect?
retry_on_non_idempotent_write.noise: Skip reads, visible upserts, connect-only retries, tests.
retry_on_non_idempotent_write.example: Celery autoretry task calls payment POST without key.

config_bulk_blast_radius.name: Single change fanned across many environments
config_bulk_blast_radius.label: AntiPattern
config_bulk_blast_radius.pitfall: One commit edits the same key across many envs with no staged rollout.
config_bulk_blast_radius.signal: >=3 env/region/service overlay files changed in one commit plus revert/fix touching same files within 7 days, or shared base with >=3 dependents; exclude bot/image-tag bumps.
config_bulk_blast_radius.question: What staging does this need?

layered_retry_amplification.name: Stacked retries across call-graph layers
layered_retry_amplification.label: AntiPattern
layered_retry_amplification.signal: Resolved CALLS path depth 2-6 crossing a network/queue boundary with >=2 retry layers; product of literal max attempts >=9 or an uncapped layer. Start with Python/Celery/requests/urllib3 and k8s backoffLimit.
layered_retry_amplification.packet: Chain with per-layer params, intro commits.
layered_retry_amplification.question: Which layer should own retries?
layered_retry_amplification.noise: Require typed edges; ignore tests and idempotent local retries.

tenant_filter_sibling_drift.name: Tenant scope dropped in sibling queries
tenant_filter_sibling_drift.label: Pattern
tenant_filter_sibling_drift.why: One unscoped sibling suffices for IDOR.
tenant_filter_sibling_drift.signal: Commit changes id-only lookup into tenant-scoped or message IDOR|cross-tenant; then grep HEAD for sibling id-only lookups on same model; no pure ratio trigger.
tenant_filter_sibling_drift.packet: Scoped/unscoped sites, fix diff, RLS/manager config.
tenant_filter_sibling_drift.question: Which lookups rely on global ids?

worker_count_vs_process_local_state.name: Worker count change vs process-local state
worker_count_vs_process_local_state.label: AntiPattern
worker_count_vs_process_local_state.signal: Fire on config transition (gunicorn workers, WEB_CONCURRENCY, pm2 instances, cluster, replicas 1->N); rank mutated module-level containers by mutation-site count in handler-like files, import proximity to entrypoint.
worker_count_vs_process_local_state.packet: Config diff, mutated globals, later fixes.
worker_count_vs_process_local_state.question: Which state is correct only for one worker?
worker_count_vs_process_local_state.example: WEB_CONCURRENCY 1 to 4 breaks in-memory job dict.

asset_cache_busting_change.name: Asset fingerprinting / service-worker versioning changed
asset_cache_busting_change.label: Pattern
asset_cache_busting_change.pitfall: Removing content hashes or editing SW lifecycle causes stale bundles.
asset_cache_busting_change.signal: Bundler/sw config: hash token removed from filename pattern, publicPath/assetPrefix/storage backend change, skipWaiting/clients.claim toggle; independent trigger: fix messages ChunkLoadError|stale bundle|cache bust; skip routine CACHE_NAME bumps.
asset_cache_busting_change.packet: Config diffs, chunk error handling, index.html cache headers.
asset_cache_busting_change.question: What deploy invariant broke?

dormant_critical_path_code.name: Awakening of dormant high-fan-in code
dormant_critical_path_code.label: AntiPattern
dormant_critical_path_code.pitfall: Old unreviewed code surprises when finally changed.
dormant_critical_path_code.signal: Symbol dormant >=2 years, modified, then fix/revert/churn within 90 days, with fan-in top 10% or new caller; no standalone dormancy.
dormant_critical_path_code.question: What hidden assumptions does it hold?
dormant_critical_path_code.example: Old Power Peg code triggered by partial deploy.

base_path_prefix_change.name: Base path / mount-prefix setting changed
base_path_prefix_change.label: Pattern
base_path_prefix_change.pitfall: Sub-path apps need the prefix consistent in many places.
base_path_prefix_change.signal: >=2 distinct prefix settings (homepage, base, basePath, root_path, FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME) change within 10 commits, or one followed by fix message within 14 days; exclude generated config and CDN-only STATIC_URL.
base_path_prefix_change.packet: Prefix lines at HEAD, diffs, proxy config.
base_path_prefix_change.question: What settings must agree?
base_path_prefix_change.example: Vite base '/app/' but nginx and OAuth left at '/'.

snapshot_blind_update.name: Blind snapshot or golden file updates
snapshot_blind_update.label: AntiPattern
snapshot_blind_update.pitfall: Snapshots regenerated en masse accept unintended changes.
snapshot_blind_update.signal: Commit with production changes plus >=10 snapshot files or >=300 lines changed, no message reason, and fix on same symbols within 30 days; sample top 5 hunks.
snapshot_blind_update.question: What change was accepted unintentionally?

hot_path_blocking_call_added.name: Blocking or remote call added to a high-fan-in function
hot_path_blocking_call_added.label: AntiPattern
hot_path_blocking_call_added.pitfall: New I/O in a commonly called function raises latency for all callers.
hot_path_blocking_call_added.why: Later cache/batch fix defines a constraint.
hot_path_blocking_call_added.signal: Diff adds network/subprocess/DB call to top-decile in-degree symbol, with follow-up within 60 days on same symbol with perf/latency/cache message (mandatory).
hot_path_blocking_call_added.question: What cost did it add and what constraint emerged?
hot_path_blocking_call_added.noise: Skip flagged/cached calls, logging, test helpers.
hot_path_blocking_call_added.example: Perf bugs cluster in commonly called code.

cache_key_design_and_bust_churn.name: CI cache key hand-busted repeatedly
cache_key_design_and_bust_churn.label: Pattern
cache_key_design_and_bust_churn.pitfall: Cache version suffixes are bumped by hand after stale caches.
cache_key_design_and_bust_churn.why: Passes on stale artifacts; poisoning risk.
cache_key_design_and_bust_churn.signal: >=2 literal version-token bumps (key v1->v2->v3, CACHE_VERSION) in 12 months, or restore-keys loosening after a break, or cache-related fix messages; missing hashFiles only as boost.
cache_key_design_and_bust_churn.question: What failure does the cache design cause?
cache_key_design_and_bust_churn.example: node cache v1->v2->v3 after 'tests pass only on fresh runner'.

csrf_exemption_and_trusted_origin_drift.name: CSRF exemption and trusted-origin accretion
csrf_exemption_and_trusted_origin_drift.label: AntiPattern
csrf_exemption_and_trusted_origin_drift.pitfall: csrf_exempt and trusted origins grow as workarounds.
csrf_exemption_and_trusted_origin_drift.why: Each exemption on cookie-auth endpoint is a hole.
csrf_exemption_and_trusted_origin_drift.signal: Nth (>=3) added exemption marker, or exemption/origin edit in commit with 403|csrf message; attach handler body; demote handlers with hmac/signature.
csrf_exemption_and_trusted_origin_drift.question: Why bypassed and what compensates?
csrf_exemption_and_trusted_origin_drift.noise: Webhooks with signatures, bearer APIs, tests.
csrf_exemption_and_trusted_origin_drift.example: csrf_exempt added to login instead of fixing trusted origins.

commented_out_code_block.name: Commented-out code block with a stated reason
commented_out_code_block.label: RejectedAttempt
commented_out_code_block.pitfall: Code is disabled with a reason and left as a rejected-approach record.
commented_out_code_block.signal: Added comment block >=3 lines that parses as code, with a reason keyword (broke|slow|disabled|causes) in block, adjacent comment or message and adjacent live replacement; survival by searching HEAD text.
commented_out_code_block.question: Why was it disabled?
commented_out_code_block.noise: Skip docstring examples, license, docs dirs, no-reason blocks.
commented_out_code_block.example: Commented batched insert with '# too slow on prod'.

satd_comment_removed_code_unchanged.name: Debt comment deleted without the debt being repaid
satd_comment_removed_code_unchanged.label: AntiPattern
satd_comment_removed_code_unchanged.pitfall: SATD comments are removed while the code is unchanged; many removals are not real repayments.
satd_comment_removed_code_unchanged.why: The warning is lost while the flaw remains.
satd_comment_removed_code_unchanged.signal: Removed SATD line whose symbol non-comment body diff is empty/<3 lines AND a fix-lineage commit on the symbol within 12 months (hard requirement); bulk/no-fix-message as ranking boosts.
satd_comment_removed_code_unchanged.packet: Removed comment, body before/after, removing commit, later fix.
satd_comment_removed_code_unchanged.question: Was the warning lost and did the later fix match its prediction?
satd_comment_removed_code_unchanged.noise: Drop deleted/moved symbols, reformat/bulk commits, comment converted to issue ref.
satd_comment_removed_code_unchanged.example: Cleanup strips '# FIXME: not thread-safe'; race fix lands 3 months later.

duplicate_effect_idempotency_fix.name: Duplicate-processing bug fixed with dedupe
duplicate_effect_idempotency_fix.label: Pattern
duplicate_effect_idempotency_fix.pitfall: Dedupe added after double effects; siblings unprotected.
duplicate_effect_idempotency_fix.why: Shows non-idempotent ops and the chosen mechanism.
duplicate_effect_idempotency_fix.signal: Fix commit with duplicate|twice|idempot|replay message adding dedupe token (UNIQUE, ON CONFLICT, SETNX, idempotency); best-effort siblings by shared decorator/base/contract key.
duplicate_effect_idempotency_fix.question: Which handlers must be idempotent?
duplicate_effect_idempotency_fix.example: Webhook gains processed_event_id while two others unguarded.

platform_text_path_class_gap.name: Encoding, line-ending or path-form handling tested only with ASCII, LF and POSIX inputs
platform_text_path_class_gap.label: AntiPattern
platform_text_path_class_gap.pitfall: A fix (or HEAD code) handles non-ASCII text, BOMs, normalisation, CRLF or missing final newline, or Windows path forms (backslash, drive letter, UNC, case, `..`, trailing slash), but all linked tests and fixtures use ASCII, LF-only strings and forward-slash relative paths.
platform_text_path_class_gap.why: Encoding, line-ending and path-form are standard equivalence partitions that authors skip by habit; the code passes on Linux CI and fails for users on Windows (cp1252 default, CRLF, backslashes). Miller's fuzz studies found crashes concentrate in unusual input classes; git autocrlf can silently rewrite fixtures and hide the class. Oracle's own history (MCP hang fix on Windows, e220ae2) shows platform defects here. Distinct from platform-config-branch-unexercised, which is about sys.platform branches: here no branch exists, the input class changes the result.
platform_text_path_class_gap.signal: Fix-backed only. Fire when a non-bulk fix hunk adds one of encoding=/errors=/newline=/normalize(/replace('\\','/')/normpath/as_posix/\r handling inside a mapped function, AND no linked test or fixture file (byte scan) contains a non-ASCII code point, a \r, a BOM or a backslash path (whichever class the fix targets). Suppress if a .gitattributes eol rule or a pathlib-only parameter explains it. Rank by fix count and by the number of file-reading call sites.
platform_text_path_class_gap.packet: Fix hunk and message; function body; test literals classed by charset max code point, line-ending class (LF, CRLF, mixed, no trailing newline, empty) and path form; fixture byte scan; .gitattributes eol rules; callers and where their text/paths originate (git emits posix, os.walk native); where results are used as keys or compared with ==; safety findings on open() without encoding.
platform_text_path_class_gap.question: Which concrete input (e.g. 'café', CJK filename, BOM file, CRLF diff, 'a\\b.py' vs 'A/B.py') would have failed before the fix, does it reach this path at runtime on Windows, and what expected result should the single test pin? Is a .gitattributes rule masking the class?
platform_text_path_class_gap.noise: Skip pure-binary handling; generated/vendored code; log formatting and markdown rendering; functions receiving only enum or regex-restricted ids or already-normalised text; pathlib.Path params that only call Path methods; callers that guarantee git-relative POSIX paths by contract; URL handling.
platform_text_path_class_gap.example: read_manifest() fixed in c3d4 to pass encoding='utf-8' and parse_diff() handles '\r\n' since e5f6; every test string is ASCII and joined with '\n'. Add a 'naïve' manifest, a CRLF diff and a no-final-newline case.
sources: Miller, Fredriksen and So, An Empirical Study of the Reliability of UNIX Utilities, CACM 1990
Python docs PEP 686 (UTF-8 mode) and io universal newlines
Repo commit e220ae2 Fix MCP hang on Windows (internal evidence)

file_mode_flip_scars.name: Executable-bit or symlink mode flips
file_mode_flip_scars.label: Pattern
file_mode_flip_scars.pitfall: Mode changes are lost on Windows/zip/COPY.
file_mode_flip_scars.signal: old_mode != new_mode (100644/100755/120000) paired with Dockerfile/CI/Makefile reference to path, or message permission denied|chmod|exec format error, or re-flip within 60 days; no bare flips.
file_mode_flip_scars.packet: Mode transitions, referencing lines, link target.
file_mode_flip_scars.question: Which scripts must stay executable?
file_mode_flip_scars.example: entrypoint.sh loses +x on Windows; container exits.

fail_open_fallback_added.name: Fail-open fallback added on error
fail_open_fallback_added.label: Pattern
fail_open_fallback_added.signal: Added return True/allow/[]/None in except/catch in symbols named auth|permission|verify|validate|check|rate|limit|quota or security-zone fix lineage; infra fail_open|failure_mode_deny false.
fail_open_fallback_added.question: Deliberately open or closed?
fail_open_fallback_added.example: Token validation returns True on identity timeout.

flag_name_recycled.name: Flag or config key re-added after removal or dormancy
flag_name_recycled.label: AntiPattern
flag_name_recycled.pitfall: A retired key is reused with new semantics, so old consumers misread it (Knight Capital).
flag_name_recycled.signal: Key lifecycle from string contracts: re-added >=7 days after last consumer removal, or dormant >=365d then new producer/consumer; name >=6 chars with project token and different default/parse expression. No type inference.
flag_name_recycled.packet: Key timeline, remove/re-add diffs, old consumers, parse code.
flag_name_recycled.question: Which consumers still assume the old meaning?
flag_name_recycled.noise: Skip same-PR revert dance, generic names, quote-only changes, tests.

dead_after_last_caller_removed.name: Function orphaned when its last caller was removed
dead_after_last_caller_removed.label: AntiPattern
dead_after_last_caller_removed.pitfall: A callee remains after its caller is deleted (lava flow).
dead_after_last_caller_removed.why: Shows whether abandonment was a rejection, replacement or accident.
dead_after_last_caller_removed.signal: Non-public, non-entry symbol with CALLS in-degree 0 at HEAD, body >=15 lines, dead >=6 months; find last-call-removal commit; require rejection/replacement language or fix history, and name not appearing as a string anywhere incl. config.
dead_after_last_caller_removed.packet: Body, removal diff, dead duration, live look-alikes.
dead_after_last_caller_removed.question: Rejected approach, replacement or accident?
dead_after_last_caller_removed.noise: Exclude dynamic dispatch, registries, CLI entrypoints, dunders, framework conventions.
dead_after_last_caller_removed.example: retry_with_jitter() went dead when HTTP client swapped.

metric_label_cardinality.name: High-cardinality metric labels
metric_label_cardinality.label: AntiPattern
metric_label_cardinality.pitfall: User/request IDs in labels create unbounded series.
metric_label_cardinality.signal: Added metric label names matching user|account|customer|tenant|session|request|trace|email|ip|uri|url (not bare id/path), or fix messages cardinality|too many series|labeldrop; exclude route-template/status labels.
metric_label_cardinality.packet: Definition diff, label source, relabel config.
metric_label_cardinality.question: Is the label space bounded?

access_scope_oscillation.name: IAM/RBAC/network access narrowed then restored
access_scope_oscillation.label: Pattern
access_scope_oscillation.pitfall: Policies are tightened then re-widened after AccessDenied, or opened broadly as quick fixes.
access_scope_oscillation.signal: IaC/policy/RBAC files: removed Action/verb/resource/cidr line re-added verbatim within 30 days; or '*'/0.0.0.0/0 added with denied|403|forbidden|cors message.
access_scope_oscillation.packet: Permission diffs, messages, SDK call symbols.
access_scope_oscillation.question: What is the minimal permission set?

import_order_pin_marker.name: Import-order pin markers and their history
import_order_pin_marker.label: Pattern
import_order_pin_marker.signal: Marker plus (IMPORTS cycle through module, or import-related fix within N commits, or bare side-effect import); drop E402 after sys.path.insert only; skip bulk lint commits.
import_order_pin_marker.question: What load order does it depend on?
import_order_pin_marker.example: gevent patch_all noqa E402 above other imports.

import_time_side_effect_lineage.name: Import-time side effects later relocated or fixed
import_time_side_effect_lineage.label: AntiPattern
import_time_side_effect_lineage.pitfall: Work at import time depends on order and fork.
